News.title: Maniac driver who killed Scots grandad after ploughing stolen Maserati into garden at 85mph jailed for 13 years
News.content:
MANIAC CAGED Maniac driver who killed Scots grandad after ploughing stolen Maserati into garden at 85mph jailed for 13 years

A MANIAC driver who ploughed a stolen Maserati through a garden at 85mph, killing a pensioner has been jailed for 13 years and six months.

John Bell, 74, suffered “non-survivable injuries” and died after he was struck by the car and pinned against the wall of the house in Broughty Ferry near Dundee on April 13 this year.



Fraser Garden, 55, admitted causing Mr Bell’s death by dangerous driving at a hearing at the High Court in Edinburgh last month.

Garden, of no fixed abode, entered a car showroom in Broughty Ferry in the early afternoon of April 13 and brazenly stole the high-powered luxury car from the forecourt.





Garden then raced the vehicle at speeds in excess of 80mph – almost three times the speed limit – through a residential area of the town in what a judge described as an “appalling episode of driving”.

Garden also ran through a red light, drove on the wrong side of the road and overtook other vehicles into the face of oncoming traffic.

The 55-year-old finally lost control of the vehicle at a bend at the junction of Forthill Road and Nursery Road, less than 750m from the showroom.

He clipped a kerb, struck a traffic island and then ploughed through a hedge into a garden where 74-year-old John Bell was doing some work for a neighbour.



Garden also struck Mr bell’s beloved dog, Charlie.

The front of the car struck the former taxi driver before pinning him against the wall of the house, leaving him with “non-survivable” injuries.

Lord Baird jailed the killer for more than 13 years today and banned him from driving for more than 56 years.

The judge said Garden’s offending was of the “utmost severity”.

He said: “From the moment you drove away from the garage, you demonstrated wicked disregard for the lives of others.



“No sentence this court can impose can possibly hope to make up for the loss Mr Bell’s family and friends have suffered.”

Advocate depute Graeme Jessop KC previously told Edinburgh High Court that just 3.3 seconds before the crash Garden had been travelling at 85mph.

When the car struck the house it was still doing 34mph.



He told the court that emergency services quickly arrived on the scene, where Mr Bell was found to have no sign of life, having suffered “multiple blunt force injuries”.

Mr Jessop said when police arrested Garden on suspicion of causing death dangerous driving he replied “sorry”.

The lawyer also told the court Garden had 90 previous convictions including “numerous” motoring offences, and that he had been under three separate disqualifications from driving on the day of the incident.

Garden admitted five charges, including theft of a motor vehicle, causing death by dangerous driving, and driving without insurance.

He also admitted driving while disqualified and failing to provide a blood sample for drugs testing.



The court heard Mr Bell had three children, 10 adult grandchildren and nine great-grandchildren.

The judge thanked Mr Bell’s family, some of whom were present in court, for submitting four separate victim impact statements.

Garden previously attended the hearing remotely from prison dressed in a green sweater.

He appeared to cover his face with his hands as the detail of his offending was read out.

Th court heard on the day of the incident, Garden had seen the unlocked red Maserati car while wandering around the forecourt and showroom area of the West End Garage in Broughty Ferry.



The vehicle belonged to the garage’s director, who had purchased it five years earlier for £70,000, and it was estimated to be worth £40,000 on the day of the incident.

Mr Jessop said the 523 brake horsepower car could go from 0-60mph in 4.6 seconds and had a top speed of 193mph.

The court was shown photos taken after the crash, which showed the front of the car crumpled beyond recognition, with Mr Jessop saying it had been “irreparably damaged”.

A member of Mr Bell’s family could be heard sobbing in the public gallery when the image was shown on the screen.

Inspector Gordon Dickson said: “Our thoughts remain with Mr Bell’s family and friends during what is still a very difficult time. We hope this outcome will bring some form of justice after a very traumatic incident.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Fraser Garden’s actions were completely reckless and he will now face the consequences.

“We remain committed to investigating all dangerous driving and will use all the tools at our disposal to hold those responsible accountable for their actions.”

News.title: Shock moment roads turn to rivers as tourist towns in Italy & Spain battered by flash floods & Europe braces for storms
News.content:
THIS is the moment a powerful flash flood turned roads into raging rivers as a massive storm batters Europe.

Shocking footage showed cars moving like boats through waterlogged streets at the charming town of Chiavari, Italy.



High water cascaded through the town with residents seen gingerly slogging through murky submerged streets on Thursday.

Meteorologists reported that a total of 126mm of rain fell on Chiavari which sits around 25 miles east of Genoa.



An urgent yellow flood warning was issued on Thursday for the wider Liguria region, which includes Genoa and Chiavari.

It is understood the warning was upgraded to Orange for the north-eastern parts of Liguria and the eastern slopes of the Po Valley.



The regions environmental protection agency, Arpal, said: “Several storm cells developed within a line of instability that crossed our region.

“These were small but particularly intense phenomena, which originated at sea and moved inland, eventually causing localized flooding.”



The risk of flooding is set to run through Friday to around 3pm local time.

Elsewhere in Italy, 250 people were evacuated from a riverside campsite in Bergamo around 8pm.

Crews acted after a mass of mud and rock began shifting on the slope directly above the site while the river below rose.



Those evacuated were taken, along with some local residents, to public halls opened up by the two councils.

It comes as Europe braces for powerful storms, which have already caused extensive damage.

Majorcans were similarly put on high alert on Thursday as officials warned for “extreme precautions” to be taken against the forecast storm.



An urgent orange weather warning was issued as tropical thunderstorms were set forecast batter the Balearic Island.

Around 75 incidents were reported as a result of the storm, the Majorca Daily Bulletin reports.

Bolts of lightning zapped frequently throughout the evening, as rain pounded the streets.

Video shows water surging from drains however the main issue was the intense wind.



Over 30 trees toppled across the holiday destination, with gusts of wind reaching 62mph in the south-central town of Porreres.

Elsewhere in Majorca, wind speeds exceeded 45 mph, and the island remains under a yellow alert for rain until Friday evening.

Aemet – The Spanish Meteorological Agency – says wild conditions are due to continue on Saturday, with thunderstorms possible.

Violent storms also hit Spain‘s Valencia region yesterday with more than 50 emergency interventions reported by local media.



Wind speeds were recorded over 62mph and muddy water ran through the streets.

The Generalitat’s Emergency Coordination Centre has warned that storms could continue bringing significant thunder and lightning.

They advise people to remain cautious.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Also over the weekend, three people were killed and two babies were injured in devastating flash floods and a landslide caused by torrential rain.

The sweeping torrent hit the village of Manzanedo de Valdueza, in the Castile and Leon region on Saturday.

News.title: I rushed home after builders made terrifying discovery – I thought it was a wind-up… then my garden became a crime scene
News.content:
GRISLY FIND I rushed home after builders made terrifying discovery – I thought it was a wind-up… then my garden became a crime scene

A COUPLE’s terrifying discovery under their patio turned their garden into a crime scene as police suspected a potential murder.

Ross and Claire Sledger were having an extension built at their home in Wye, Kent, in 2019 when builders unearthed human bones on site.



These included a femur, two skulls, ribs and part of a pelvis, with fragments of a humerus and finger bones also uncovered.

Ten police officers scrambled to the house to investigate what they initially feared was a murder scene.



Mr Sledger, 49, says the couple moved out of their home while officers carried out excavation works for three days.

“Builders were doing our extension and Claire called me to say they’ve found some bones and my first thought was it was someone’s pet,” he recalled.

“A builder had actually found several, but it wasn’t until we saw a femur which raised alarm bells as you could see it was human.

“By the following day we had 24/7 observation on the site because they thought it could be a murder scene.



“Police were just sieving top soil, but when you have five police cars outside your house in a little village word did get around quite quickly.

“We ended up leaving the house so those investigating could get on with it. We went to a friend’s house and that’s when we were told on the phone they found a second body on the third day.”

Six years on, the bones were revealed to be Anglo-Saxon and are thought to be about 1,000 years old.

A service was held at St Gregory and St Martin Church in the village where the bones were laid to rest in the graveyard.

More than 25 people attended the service at St Gregory and St Martin Church, which began with the singing of William Blake’s Jerusalem.



Reverend Ravi Holy, rector of the church, confirmed the identities of both bodies remain unknown, but said villagers should still have the opportunity to pay their respects.

“Ross and Claire are a lovely couple in the village and it was obviously a shock to them,” he said.

“But once we knew more information and discovered they were Anglo-Saxon bones, we wanted to do something and that’s why we’ve had the service.



“I’m absolutely delighted with the turnout and how it’s gone. Everyone who lives in Wye is generally proud of living here and they enjoy their history.”

Local historians say Bridge Street had been developed for housing in the 1930s, and a number of skeletons were found during that work.

Mrs Sledger, 48, who runs The Sawyers bar in Bridge Street, says their neighbour had also discovered a sword and other bones shortly after the 2019 discovery.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

When asked how she feels about the bones being laid to rest, she said: “It’s taken a long time to discover what they were and whether they were going to be archived.

“It’s been a lovely service and knowing the bones will be in the churchyard is nice so everyone can pay their respects here, rather than at our house.”

News.title: Baby girl found dead strapped in car seat after ‘grandma forgot nursery drop-off and left her in vehicle for 8 hours’
News.content:
CAR HORROR Baby girl found dead strapped in car seat after ‘grandma forgot nursery drop-off and left her in vehicle for 8 hours’

A BABY died after her grandmother left her inside a blistering hot car for eight hours instead of dropping her off at daycare, it has been alleged.

Scottie Gwyn Crowell, who was only 10-months-old, was found strapped in the backseat of the vehicle, where temperatures had reached 46C.



Her grandmother, Dr Stacey Fazenbaker, had offered to pick her up from home and drive her to daycare in Madisonville, Kentucky.

When Scottie’s father went to pick her up at 4pm on August 13, staff told him that she was never dropped off that morning, the Daily Mail reported.



The family quickly learned that Fazenbaker had instead gone straight to work at Owensboro Health Multicare – and forgotten the little girl in the car, WEHT reported.

Madisonville Police Major Jason McKnight said Fazenbaker “ran outside with some co-workers to get the child” – but it was already too late.

Read more about Kentucky GUN HORROR One dead and two kids among multiple injured in shooting at outdoor concert



“Officers arrived on scene, Med Center and the fire department arrived shortly after they did and they found the infant,” he said.

“The grandmother had already got the child, and the officers tried some lifesaving measures, but unfortunately it was too late for that.”

He added: “Anybody who loses a child obviously is going to be very upset, and this is no different.

“So yes, the families were all there and more came, after the fact. But yes, for this community, it’s a pretty big deal.”



Fazenbaker was tested for drugs and alcohol, but police do not anticipate positive results.

No charges have been filed as officers continue to investigate the case.

McKnight added: “As the picture becomes clearer on how this could have possibly happened, there is a possibility charges are sought before the grand jury convenes.”

An autopsy was carried out to determine the cause of death. The results will be available in several weeks.

Tributes have poured in for Scottie, describing her as a “beautiful and precious angel that was taken way too soon.”



“I do not know Scottie personally, but I felt like I did through her mom,” read one of the heartfelt messages in an online obituary book made by the baby’s parents.

“Dr Crowell has helped me as my OB/ GYN in so many ways. My heart breaks for the family and I pray you find peace in the coming days. Scottie was such a beautiful miracle.”

News.title: Woman, 38, who posed as 12-year-old girl using child’s voice & carrying teddy to trick family into adoption is jailed
News.content:
TWISTED DECEPTION Woman, 38, who posed as 12-year-old girl using child’s voice & carrying teddy to trick family into adoption is jailed

A CREEPY fraudster who pretended to be a 12-year-old girl has been jailed for tricking families into adopting her.

Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira, 37, was convicted of fraud and using a false identity to deceive a couple into taking her in for 14 months.



The court heard how Oliveira conned a couple by posing as a traumatised child – using a childlike voice, dummies and baby bottles to maintain her deception.

They found she deliberately created a fake identity and sentenced her to a total of one year, 10 months and 28 days in jail.



The twisted case was heard in Joinville, Brazil, with testimony from the couple who took her in, along with police and other experts.

The couple treated her like a daughter, giving her accommodation, money, food, medication, and other care.

Oliveira also scammed the couple into giving her a bedroom filled with toys and throwing her a “12th birthday party” – despite being 38.

She initially introduced herself as an 18-year-old called “Gabriele”, saying she had experience in baking and was looking for work.



After gaining the couple’s trust, she changed her story, claiming that she was actually 11-years-old and had suffered abuse and abandonment.

Oliveira claimed to have autism and other health problems, saying her adult appearance was because she had been “forced to take hormones during childhood”.

The couple also paid for her weight-loss treatment using the prescription drug tirzepatide.

She deceived the couple to obtain “the full cost of her own subsistence”, the court heard.

The judge said she had acted consciously “to induce and maintain the victims in error” in order to obtain material benefits through the false identity.



The case unravelled when a relative of the couple became suspicious of Oliveira and found reports online of previous cases in Brazil involving her.

Cops were contacted at the end of May and Oliveira was arrested at their home on June 2.

During questioning, she told police that she was actually from Ceara not Para, while also admitting to using a false name and age.

Evidence from the trial included a forensic examination of her phone, statements from victims and witnesses, and her own admission that she used false personal details.

Investigators were also able to link Oliveira to similar alleged scams in at least seven Brazilian states, including São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.



During the Covid-19 pandemic, she allegedly posed as “Emily” – a 13-year-old girl suffering from terminal leukaemia.

One woman reportedly had the name “Emily” tattooed on her wrist after becoming emotionally attached to what she believed to be a child.

Another case in 2017 involved social worker Delma Soares, who said Oliveira stayed with her in Belo Horizonte after posing as a vulnerable teenager called Karolina.

Delma said: “She liked to wear children’s clothes with childish designs.”

Oliveira reportedly arrived with injuries caused by needles and wire, with hospital examinations finding objects in her body.



Another alleged victim, nutritionist Renata Magalhaes, detailed how Oliveira maintained the scam saying: “Her phone was full of searches [on] how an autistic person behaves and how to make drawings to move evangelical people.

“She is a person who puts on a character like a coat and creates a totally fake narrative.”

Renata also alleged that Amanda swallowed needles and later vomited them in front of her.

Oliveira previously denied intending to defraud anyone, saying: “It is clear that I deceived people, I lied.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Her defence argued that her identities were a survival tactic, not a deliberate fraud.



Oliveira’s lawyer Lucio Sousa described her actions as “the way she found to survive”.

News.title: Boy, 2, dies after being pulled unresponsive from swimming pool as devastated family pay tribute to ‘joy of our life’
News.content:
POOL TRAGEDY Boy, 2, dies after being pulled unresponsive from swimming pool as devastated family pay tribute to ‘joy of our life’

A TODDLER has tragically died after being pulled unconscious from a pool in Texas.

Two-year-old Malachi Israel LeBlanc was swimming in a community pool in San Antonio when he was found unresponsive in the water.



Bystanders desperately tried to save him life by giving him CPR before he was rushed to the local hospital on August 5.

The toddler was declared brain dead days later and died on August 9.



The Bexar County Medical Examiner’s Office ruled Malachi’s death an accident.

His grieving parents, Grace and Myron decided to donate their son’s organs.

His mom admitted being initially hesitant about the idea: “My initial thing was, not my baby, nobody’s going to cut my baby open.”

But she thought about other families praying for a miracle for their children, just like she did with Malachi, and it changed her mind.

“I’ve been in that room praying for a miracle, wanting my baby to live.”

“I felt that pain.”



“To know that other parents are going through that, and there’s a chance that they’ll get to hear their baby cry again, that they’ll get to feel their breath and listen to their heartbeat – absolutely, why would I not want to give them that?”

The organs that are likely to be donated are his heart, liver and kidneys, depending on the transplant’s success, according to his family.

Donate Life America believes his type of donation is rare.

The charity said that over 2,200 children under 18 are currently on the national waiting list for transplants.

27 per cent of those in need of healthy organs are under the age of 5.



His father Myron posted on Facebook: “Those babies who receive Malachi’s organs will get a chance at life.”

“Those families will receive a blessing that our Lord has provided for them through Malachi.”

“His story, and the way it has touched so many people, will live on.”

“I am honoured to have been trusted with such a son as Malachi.”

“In two short years, he touched so many people.”



“Everywhere he went, he brought a smile to someone’s face.”

“Everyone was always telling me how beautiful he was and what a joy it was to be around him.”

According to Malachi’s GoFundMe page, which will help cover funeral expenses, it has been said that three children in Texas will receive the Malachi’s organs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The page’s organiser, Michael Mejia, posted an update, announcing that there will be a night of worship, in San Antonio on August 21, to “honor the life of sweet Malachi LeBlanc.”

So far, collected donations are now just under $25,000 , with the final target being $65,000.

News.title: When will the A31 reopen and why is it still closed after wildfire?
News.content:
MOTORISTS across Hampshire and Dorset face continued travel disruption as a major stretch of the A31 through the New Forest remains shut following a 100-hectare wildfire.

National Highways and emergency services have been working to repair severe structural damage caused by the fire, which burned ancient woodland and heathland alongside the busy dual carriageway.



Here is everything drivers need to know about when the road will reopen, what caused the closure, and why repairs are taking so long.

How did the wildfire start?

The incident began on August 9, when a vehicle caught fire along the roadside near Ringwood.



Fanned by dry summer conditions, flames quickly jumped from the burning vehicle into adjacent heathland and open countryside.

The fire burned across 1.6 square kilometres – equivalent to more than 140 football pitches – destroying rare natural habitats and ancient trees that had stood for centuries.



At the height of the blaze, more than 160 fire engines and crews from 93 stations used tens of millions of litres of water to tackle the wildfire.

Why is the road taking so long to reopen?

While the main flames are extinguished, reopening the road is more complicated than simply sweeping away ash.

National Highways discovered extensive structural damage once emergency teams granted safe access to the site.

Extreme heat damaged large stretches of the tarmac, and contractors have had to carry out extensive resurfacing before the carriageway is safe for vehicles.



Several hundred metres of steel vehicle restraint barriers were also destroyed by the intense heat, and must be replaced.

And in the New Forest, replacing boundary fencing is vital, as without it, free-roaming ponies, cattle, and donkeys could wander onto the 70mph dual carriageway.

When will the A31 reopen?

National Highways currently expects the A31 to remain closed in both directions between Junction 2 of the M27 and Picket Post (A338) until at least Saturday, August 22.

But transport bosses say the exact reopening date depends on completing final safety checks and essential infrastructure repairs.

Highways teams are pushing to finish works ahead of the weekend, but driver safety remains the priority before barriers can be lifted.



Firefighters are continuing to inspect the scorched ground using specialist off-road vehicles, dampening down hidden embers to prevent sudden flare-ups.

Officials urge drivers to allow extra journey time, check traffic updates, and ensure vehicles are carrying extra water and sufficient fuel during hot weather delays.

News.title: Migrant fiends raped woman at knifepoint as she stargazed in park on first date with another man
News.content:
HORROR ATTACK Migrant fiends raped woman at knifepoint as she stargazed in park on first date with another man

TWO migrants raped a woman at knifepoint as she stargazed in a park on a first date with another man.

Afghan nationals Khan Agah, 19 and Noorullah Ahmdzai, 26, treated their victim as an “object they could use and abuse”.

The vile pair pounced on the woman in Barking Park, East London, on August 16 last year.

Ahmdzai raped her while Agah held a Swiss Army-type knife to her date’s throat.





He threatened to kill him if he tried to call the police before the fiends switched roles.

Nutan Fatania, prosecuting, said: “This was a terrifying knife-point rape at the hands of these two defendants on two strangers.

“The complainants had met for the first time that day and they were laying down on each other with a guitar, star gazing, when these two men approached them and overpowered them.

“They viewed the woman they came across as an object they could use and abuse.



“She was not a human being to them, she was an object they were entitled to violate, but she was not an object, she was real human being subjected to a harrowing attack.”

Agah and Ahmdzai were convicted of two counts of rape, two charges of threatening with a knife, as well as one offence of assault by penetration and one of false imprisonment.

Snaresbrook Crown Court heard the victim had agreed to meet her partner after they began messaging on a dating app two weeks before.

As she lay down in his arms under the stars, Agah and Ahmdzai ambushed the couple.



Following the horror attack, both men sickeningly tried to claim the woman was a sex worker.

Their web of lies meant the victim broke down and was forced to take a break after being grilled during her evidence.

Ahmdzai came to Britain on a small boat in August 2023 and was housed in a hotel in London by the Home Office at the taxpayer’s expense, before being moved to Liverpool.

While in Liverpool his claim for asylum was rejected and he began working at a building site to pay for an appeal and returned to London.

Agah also came to the UK illegally but how he arrived remains unclear.



Detective Constable Megan Lelliott, who led the investigation, said: “This was a horrific ordeal for the victim who has been exceptionally brave in not only reporting what happened to her, but also reliving the whole experience during the trial.

“Her courage means two dangerous men will be held accountable for their actions.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We remain committed to thoroughly investigating all reports of rape and sexual offences, while providing every support to those who come forward.”

Both predators will be sentenced in October.

News.title: Billy Caldwell turns 21 - the boy who legalised medicinal cannabis in Britain
News.content:
The mum of the boy who changed UK law on medicinal cannabis has told of his miraculous recovery as he turns 21.

Billy Caldwell had been placed on palliative care as a 12-year-old due to having up to 800 seizures a day before mum Charlotte took him to Canada where he was prescribed a medicine that would save his life. He has just celebrated his landmark birthday and is now seizure free for three years.

Billy made headlines in 2018 when UK Border Force confiscated his cannabis oil on their return at Heathrow Airport. His case sparked a fierce debate about access to the drug for the chronically ill, resulting in the Home Office returning his medicine and legalising it for medical use.

View 6 Images Charlotte with Billy in hospital back in 2018

‌



Teen faces life-threatening epileptic seizures after NHS refuses to fund cannabis drug READ MORE :

“It’s quite incredible that he’s reached this milestone,” Charlotte told the Mirror. “I never thought I’d get to say that he’s celebrating his 21st birthday. I didn’t think he would make it to 21.”

Billy Caldwell’s landmark case sparked debate around how the “war on drugs” had prevented clinical trials from being carried out to investigate potential benefits of cannabis in some forms.

View 6 Images Billy enjoying the beach and on his birthday

Back in 2018 Charlotte publicised the fact that she and Billy planned to return to the UK from Toronto - carrying the medicine that was illegal here. She said “I was crying and one of the customs officers who took his cannabis oil was crying. He said ‘I’m a father myself but I’ve got to do my job’.”

‌



Billy’s epilepsy was so severe that he was being tube-fed and struggled to stand. Charlotte hosted a media briefing in a hotel lobby in central London to tell reporters that he would die if the cannabis oil was not returned to him.

Charlotte, from County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, said: “I had been offered palliative care for Billy. He was having between 300 to 800 seizures a day and the doctors told me that was his new baseline and that EEG scans of his brain were ‘lighting up like a Christmas tree’.

View 6 Images Charlotte speaking to the media outside hospital in 2018 (Image: Steve Bainbridge)

“He was having seizures every few minutes. I was sent home from hospital with him seizing. I couldn’t stomach the thought of palliative care so I took my little boy home to die. While he was asleep I researched anything that could help him and came across medical cannabis.”

‌



Charlotte says that while Billy, who has autism, still requires around the clock care, his life has been transformed. She said: “Billy is not just surviving but thriving. All my dreams for Billy are coming true. Prescription cannabis has given him a life.

“Before he accessed prescription cannabis he was struggling to stay awake, he was so depleted from constant seizures. I would be awake until the sun came up in case I woke up to find my boy cold and blue beside me. He could have died if he had a seizure and I didn’t see it.

View 6 Images Billy now as a 'thriving' 21 year old

“Now Billy is running around full of mischief, fun and laughter. He’s living his best life and loves horse riding, swimming and reading Harry Potter. I’m so proud of him. He was just a little boy and he took on the British government and won.”

‌



Charlotte’s gamble paid off and forced a U-turn out of then-Home Secretary Sajid Javid. He announced that he would make it legal for specialist doctors to prescribe cannabis derived medicines in certain circumstances.

However Charlotte stresses that only a tiny number of similar patients were ever granted NHS prescriptions for medicinal cannabis as experts still point to a lack of robust clinical trial data - a legacy of the fact such trials were outlawed for so long.

View 6 Images Charlotte says the system is still not working for those who most need medicinal cannabis

The law change has opened the door for medical firms to sell “whole plant” medicinal cannabis in the UK but she says many users able to pay the cost of up to £1,000 a month are not those vulnerable and chronically ill, such as Billy.

‌



Charlotte said: “These are people who often can’t work because of their illness. They can’t afford this. Thousands of people who really need this type of medication still cannot access it.”

News.title: Harry facing initial bill of up to £10m along with others after losing court battle with Daily Mail
News.content:
Harry facing initial bill of up to £10m along with others after losing court battle with Daily Mail

The Duke of Sussex and six other household names are set to discover how many millions of pounds they must pay towards the legal costs after losing the high-profile privacy lawsuit

View 5 Images Days after his return to Britain was confirmed, Prince Harry will learn how many millions of pounds he will have ‌to pay towards the legal costs (Image: Getty Images)

Prince Harry will soon to find out how many millions he must initially stump up to the Daily Mail’s publisher in legal costs after his failed High Court case.

‌



The Duke of Sussex and high-profile figures including Sir Elton John, Elizabeth Hurley and Baroness Doreen Lawrence, sued Associated Newspapers Limited over allegations of unlawful information-gathering. The group strongly denied the claims which were heard at a trial in London earlier this year, with judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissing all the cases in a judgment on July 7.

‌



The cases returned to the High Court for a two-day hearing over costs, where the court was told ANL’s total costs were more than £34 million. The group, which also publishes the Mail On Sunday, had asked for more than £9.9 million as an interim payment ahead of future hearings to decide its legal costs in depth.

‌



View 5 Images Elton John and husband David Furnish are also awaiting the legal bill this afternoon (Image: WWD via Getty Images)

Prince Harry's return reason revealed as Meghan Markle offered huge UK role READ MORE :

Prince Harry must wait on security decision as officials deal with protecting nine ex-Prime Ministers READ MORE :

Mr Justice Nicklin is now due to give his decision on the size of an initial payment the group will make to ANL, as well as how the full costs will be assessed.

The judgment comes after it was made public on Wednesday that Harry and his wife the Duchess of Sussex are moving back to the UK.

‌



The couple decamped to California more than six years ago amid the Megxit crisis but now will relocate back from the US to the UK later this month to live in a non-royal residence outside London.

5 View 5 Images Elizabeth Hurley also brought a case against the publishers (Image: PA) 5 View 5 Images Mr Justice Nicklin’s judgment is expected at 2pm this afternoon (Image: Avalon)

‌



Lawyers for the group of household names, also including David Furnish, Sadie Frost, and Sir Simon Hughes, said the interim payment should be just over £7.9 million.

Mr Justice Nicklin previously said the claimants would need to pay the interim payment on August 28, adding: “They are going to be paying a sum of money that I will confirm in the judgment.”

View 5 Images Doreen Lawrence, the mother of murdered Stephen Lawrence, lost the case (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

During the hearing, ANL said the group of household names should pay the total costs on an indemnity rather than a standard basis, which would be more favourable to the publisher in terms of the amount it can recover.

However, Nicholas Bacon KC, for the group, said in written submissions that it could be “very significant” if the group of seven had to pay ANL’s costs on this stricter basis and could lead to them being without enough insurance cover.

Mr Justice Nicklin’s written judgment is expected at 2pm.

News.title: Passport Office shares 'don't travel' advice as trips could be 'disrupted'
News.content:
Passport Office shares 'don't travel' advice as trips could be 'disrupted'

The travel advice was shared to help prevent disruptions for people with upcoming trips

View 2 Images People should be aware of the travel guidance (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

HM Passport Office (HMPO) has shared essential travel advice for anyone travelling abroad. The alert comes amid the busy summer holiday period, when countless families are planning trips.

‌



In a post shared on social media, HMPO urged people not to travel with a passport that they had previously reported lost or stolen. The X alert said: "Found a passport you previously reported lost or stolen? Don’t travel with it. Once reported, it’s cancelled and using it could disrupt your trip."

‌



Instead, they will need to apply for a replacement. HM Passport Office says it considers passports damaged if any of your details cannot be read, any of the pages are ripped or cut, there are holes in the cover, the cover is coming away, or there are stains on the pages. For instance, ink or water damage is not allowed.

‌



HM Passport Office says it is important to cancel a lost or stolen passport as soon as you can. "This will reduce the risk of anyone else using your passport or your identity.

"You can report a lost or stolen passport for someone else if they cannot do it themselves." If you have a photo of the lost passport, you can use this to answer the necessary questions.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The advice continues: "You might be able to apply for an emergency travel document. You’ll need to pay a fee. If you apply for an emergency travel document, you do not need to cancel your passport now. You’ll cancel it as part of your application for the emergency travel document."

When renewing your passport online, you will need a credit or debit card and a digital photo. It costs £102. If you are replacing a lost or stolen passport, you also need someone to confirm your identity online. More details are available on GOV.UK.

You can also follow @HM_Passport on X for general updates and tips. For instance, another recent post shares tips for taking your passport photos. The advice said: "A suitable passport photo can help avoid delays. Make sure your photo is in focus, against a plain background and meets all requirements."

Article continues below

View 2 Images HMPO shared the advice in a social media post (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

GOV.UK says: "In your photo you must: be facing forwards and looking straight at the camera, have a plain expression and your mouth closed, have your eyes open and visible, not have hair in front of your eyes, not have a head covering (unless it’s for religious or medical reasons).

"Do not have anything covering your face, not have any shadows on your face or behind you."

News.title: 'I died for an hour – I'm convinced there's something beyond life after being sent back'
News.content:
'I died for an hour – I'm convinced there's something beyond life after being sent back'

Eduardo says he died for 60 minutes, and doctors feared the worst, but claims he came back with a new mission and a story about what he believes was a brush with the afterlife

View 3 Images A Spanish man spoke about what he believes was a near-death experience (NDE) (Image: fenix_eduardomj/Instagram)

A Spanish man who returned from the brink after his heart stopped has spoken about the profound impact of what he believes was a near-death experience (NDE). Instagram user Eduardo (@fenix_eduardomj) says he died for 60 minutes — and doctors feared the worst. But he claims he came back with a new "mission" and a story about what he believes was a glimpse of the afterlife.

‌



Speaking in a video for his social media accounts that has drawn much attention online, he said: "In February last year, 2025, when I was 34, my heart stopped for an hour."

‌



Eduardo said that before his near-death experience, he'd been in good health and regularly played tennis. But it was after a game that he began to feel unwell — setting the stage for the terrifying incident that followed.

‌



He chose to head to the hospital, but he deteriorated. Once there, he was placed on a stretcher. He went into cardiac arrest three times, and doctors worked to revive him.

View 3 Images Eduardo says he died for 60 minutes (Image: fenix_eduardomj/Instagram)

"I woke up the next day in the ICU, and that's when I began to remember what I’d seen in the afterlife." Eduardo later shed light on his most notable experiences.

‌



He explained that he'd been with his late grandfather and had also found himself in a courtroom, where "they told me I couldn’t stay there, that I had to go back because I hadn’t completed my mission."

Eduardo, who's adamant that it wasn't a dream, claims that at one point, he was in the sky above an ambulance. Inside, he says he was unconscious, and his heart had stopped.

He recalled: "I was unconscious inside the ambulance. Whilst being transferred from one hospital to another, my heart stopped, and that’s when your soul, spirit or consciousness leaves your body, and you can see yourself."

‌



Eduardo later learned that, while unconscious, he had been taken to a different hospital. He said it became the defining part of the experience, proof, to him, that there is "something beyond life."

View 3 Images Eduardo believes he "had to come back" (Image: fenix_eduardomj/Instagram)

He added that, during the courtroom experience, his grandfather, who had died two decades earlier, was next to him. He said others then deliberated over whether he should be sent back to the living.

‌



Once it was decided that he should go back, Eduardo found himself feeling unable to return as his "whole body ached", but his grandfather helped him through the use of what was described as a type of wind.

"It was a very brief experience, but it felt very real. I was at peace; I didn't miss life", he explained.

Eduardo eventually woke up and asked whether he’d been taken to hospital with a police escort — something he couldn’t have known, as he was unconscious at the time — leaving his family stunned.

Article continues below

He believes he "had to come back" because he "hadn’t been doing what I really wanted to do for five years". Eduardo says this was to continue the legacy of Spanish nature presenter Félix Rodríguez de la Fuente.

Eduardo has since launched the "Phoenix Project" to pursue his goals, teaching people how to be happy so they can better care for animals and the environment.

He said: "My mission is to build the @‌fenix_society_ project, an initiative to drive us all to fight for our dreams and live in alignment with who we truly are, so that we may live in harmony with everything around us."

News.title: Families save £1.28billion in Inheritance Tax by leaving gifts to charity
News.content:
Families save £1.28billion in Inheritance Tax by leaving gifts to charity

The amount of Inheritance Tax saved through charitable gifts is up 88% over the last five years, from £680million

View 2 Images Inheritance Tax is normally due on estates that are worth over £325,000 but there are several rules in place that can increase this (Image: Getty)

Families saved £1.28billion in Inheritance Tax last year by leaving gifts to charity in their wills, according to a law firm.

‌



Inheritance Tax has to be paid after someone has died if the value of their estate - including money, property, and possessions - are worth over £325,000. The standard rate that is charged is 40% on the value above this amount.

‌



But new data from TWM Solicitors shows the amount of Inheritance Tax saved through charitable gifts is up 88% over the last five years, from £680million. Gifts to charity are exempt from Inheritance Tax.

‌



In addition, where 10% or more of an estate is left to charity then the remaining taxable estate benefits from a reduced Inheritance Tax rate of 36%, compared with the standard 40%. HMRC figures show this reduced-rate relief saved estates £55million in Inheritance Tax last year.

View 2 Images More people are using charity donations to reduce their Inheritance Tax bill (Image: Getty)

Gillian Dunlea, Managing Associate at TWM Solicitors, said leaving charitable gifts is often driven by personal reasons but adds that many families do not realise that it can reduce Inheritance Tax.

‌



She said: “Some people are understandably concerned about the level of IHT payable on their estates, and charitable giving can appeal because gifts to charity are free from IHT.”

“With pensions being subject to IHT from 2027, pensions may become less tax efficient for families to inherit, so clients should review their pension nominations alongside their wills, particularly where they intend to make charitable gifts as part of overall estate planning.”

“Many charities are under increasing financial pressure and legacy gifts do play an important role in supporting their long-term work. For some charities, larger gifts left in wills can be transformative.”

‌



Get the best deals and tips from Mirror Money WHATSAPP GROUP: Get money news and top deals straight to your phone by joining our Money WhatsApp group here. We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

In the UK, fewer than 5% of estates trigger an Inheritance Tax bill. This is because there are several rules and allowances that are in place that can actually boost your tax-free threshold.

For example, there is no Inheritance Tax due on any gifts if you live for seven years after giving them - unless the gift is part of a trust.

Article continues below

There is also no Inheritance Tax to pay when an estate is left to your spouse or civil partner. If you give away your home to your children or grandchildren, then you get an additional £175,000 allowance.

This therefore increases your overall Inheritance Tax threshold to £500,000. If you are married or in a civil partnership, any Inheritance Tax allowance that isn’t used can be passed on when someone dies.

This means a couple can potentially pass on as much as £1million without their estate being subject to Inheritance Tax.

News.title: Teacher 'kissed pupil, locked her in a cupboard and supplied her with drugs'
News.content:
Teacher 'kissed pupil, locked her in a cupboard and supplied her with drugs'

Lee Nicholson, a former physics teacher at Aston Academy in Rotherham, had an inappropriate relationship with a a pupil who he kissed and sent sexually explicit messages, a tribunal heard

View Image Lee Nicholson was a physics teacher at Aston Academy (Image: Google Maps )

A teacher sent sexually explicit messages to a pupil he kissed and locked in a cupboard, a teaching tribunal heard.

‌



Lee Nicholson, a former physics teacher at Aston Academy in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, engaged in an inappropriate relationship with the pupil between 2014 and 2018, a hearing by the Teacher Regulation Agency found on August 10.

‌



A panel was told that the 39-year-old spent "excessive one-on-one time" with the girl, holding her hand and cuddling her, as the relationship developed.

‌



Nicholson would also message the pupil sexually explicit conduct, lock her in a cupboard and kiss her, it was claimed. On other occasions it was said he would also lock them both in a meeting room.

Met Office maps show 79 UK counties face heavy rain and thunderstorms on Tuesday READ MORE :

In the hearing it was also said that Nicholson encouraged the pupil to take recreational drugs and gave her gifts and presents. they would meet at 7am before school began and on Saturdays in 2016, when she was preparing for her exams.

South Yorkshire Police arrested Nicholson in March 2023 on suspicion of inciting a girl under 16 to engage in sexual activity. During a search of his home, officers found drugs.

‌



In April 2024, he was convicted and fined at Sheffield Magistrates' Court on four offences relating to the possession of various drugs, including cocaine, reported YorkshireLive.

The school suspended Nicholson pending investigation when he was arrested. In January 2024, it commenced an internal investigation into the allegations and Nicholson left employment on April 29, 2024.

Nicholson provided the pupil with a desk in the cupboard where she was locked while he was teaching younger pupils. She told the hearing that "between lessons Mr Nicholson would come and visit her in there and they would lie together on the floor and cuddle in the far left corner of the room."

‌



In messages, Nicholson allegedly told the student to use a penis-shaped lolly in a fridge "as a dildo" and encouraged her to masturbate. The student claimed that Nicholson encouraged her to explore sexually and referred to masturbation as an "experiment".

He also is claimed to have encouraged her to take recreational drugs. The student told the police during their investigation: "When I was about 16 he spoke to me a lot about drugs, like different types of drugs and their effect in a very positive way, like I'm not very clued up on stuff like that anyway and he discussed them in a way with me that felt like he was encouraging me to take them."

The panel heard that Nicholson told her he would "drive his car off the road" and had a "suicide note" in his drawer if anyone found out about their relationship.

Article continues below

Decision maker Stuart Blomfield concluded that there was "no doubt whatsoever that such actions were in fundamental breach of the professional boundaries between a teacher and a child and in particular breached the absolutely core requirements of safeguarding and acting in the child's best interests and pursuing a child-centred approach".

Nicholson was banned from the teaching profession indefinitely.

News.title: 'Strong police presence' expected at M9 crash victim's funeral as cops clamp down on stunt drivers
News.content:
'Strong police presence' expected at M9 crash victim's funeral as cops clamp down on stunt drivers

Joe Carthy, Jack Kennedy, Alex McCarthy, Jeremy O'Brien and Kamil Pustkowski all died on Sunday when they drove a BMW into an incoming car near Moone in County Kildare

View 7 Images The scene of the crash on the M9 northbound in Co Kildare (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

A "strong policing presence" is expected at the funerals of three of the teenagers killed when they drove down the wrong way on the M9 in Ireland.

‌



Joe Carthy, 15, Jack Kennedy, 17, Alex McCarthy, 17, Jeremy O'Brien, 18, and Kamil Pustkowski, 17, all died at the scene on Sunday when they drove a BMW into an incoming car near Moone in County Kildare. Three adult sisters aged in their 20s and 30s and a seven-year-old boy remain in hospital with serious injuries.

‌



Two of the teenagers' funerals are due to take place today, with another to follow on Monday. The first service will be Carthy, from Athy in County Kildare, with the burial due this morning in Athy.

‌



Security operations will be in place at the funerals, it has now been revealed, with the Garda Public Order Unit part of the plans. The unit, commonly known as the Garda Riot Squad, deals with public disorder and civil unrest.

Joyriders crash after speeding wrong way down motorway days after deadly M9 collision READ MORE :

View 7 Images Joe Carthy

Additional officers are also expected to be deployed from across Kildare and Carlow, focusing on teenagers attempting to perform dangerous stunts during the funeral processions on scramblers or other vehicles. A source told the Irish Independent: "Gardaí have to balance the sensitivities of a funeral service with public order policing.

‌



"There won’t be a completely overt presence, but if you have a situation where young lads begin driving recklessly and doing wheelies or anything of the sort, there are resources in place to deal with that, which include the public order unit."

Earlier this week, the funeral notice for Carthy was removed from RIP.ie after a flood of angry and abusive comments appeared in its online condolences section. This afternoon, the funeral for McCarthy is due to take place in Carlow, where he was from.

A service for O'Brien, who was the driver of the BMW and is also from Carlow, is scheduled for Monday. Funeral details for Kennedy, from Athy, County Kildare, and Pustkowski, from Limerick, have not been revealed.

‌



View 7 Images Jack Kennedy

‌



Gardai said the car was driven in excess of 74mph on the wrong side of the rural motorway. Videos have emerged captioned "last spin boys", which reportedly show the teens driving a BMW on a main road.

Detectives said the car involved in the crash was purchased legitimately by an associate of the teenagers a week earlier for €1,100 (£940). Tributes shared of the five teenagers posted online showed pictures of them wearing balaclavas and committing crimes like break-ins and car thefts.

Kennedy was arrested last month in Carlow following a hit-and-run which resulted in a motorcyclist being run over by teenagers in a Ford Ranger truck. He was released without charge.

‌



O'Brien was investigated by the police for taking part in a traveller feud and was also part of a road range incident investigation last month, in which a man was assaulted with a slash hook. Pustkowski was charged with a number of offences and, as part of his bail conditions, was not allowed to leave Limerick.

View 7 Images Jeremy O'Brien (Image: Facebook)

The charges he faced included being a passenger in a stolen car, with his TikTok profile featuring videos of cars being driven the wrong way on motorways to escape officers.

‌



7 View 7 Images Kamil Pustkowski 7 View 7 Images Alex McCarthy

Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella, both in their 30s and from Carlow, and Ella Hendricken, in her 20s, have been identified as the three sisters who were seriously injured in the crash. Niamh and Alma are understood to have been in the front of the vehicle and remain in a critical condition in Tallaght Hospital, while Ella is in St Vincent’s Hospital in a serious condition.

‌



Ella and the child were in the back of the car when the collision occurred near Moone shortly before 3am. The innocent family, from the Graigecullen area of Co Carlow, are understood to have been on their way to Dublin Airport where they were making their way to a wedding abroad.

A fundraiser set up for the family on Tuesday has already amassed more than €630,000 from almost 22,000 donations. The page, set up by Bryan Curley, reads: "Hi, my name is Bryan and I’m setting up this fundraiser for my best friend Ella and her sisters, Niamh and Alma, who were recently involved in a serious road traffic accident.

"This has been an incredibly difficult and frightening time for Ella, Niamh, Alma and their family. They are facing a long and challenging road ahead."

‌



View 7 Images Ella Hendricken, Niamh Kinsella and Alma Kinsella

A similar incident occurred on the M50 in Dublin's Ballymun areas at around 3.30am on Thursday, when a group of joyriders drove the wrong way down the motorway. The car was then found crashed and abandoned, with no other vehicles were involved, after the driver failed to stop when instructed to do so by Gardaí.

This and the M9 incident come after nine people were injured in a head-on collision on the M50 in Dublin with a car travelling in the wrong direction on the motorway the previous weekend. GRA vice-president John Joe O’Connell said on Monday that there were "numerous gangs" of boys and young men "trying to outdo each other" in social media videos depicting interactions with Gardaí, pursuits and wrong-way driving.

Article continues below

Stating that his officers would no longer pursue such riders, he added: "Our members are not going to follow down that route – we’re damned if you do and damned if you don’t, that way."

Mr O’Connell criticised those partaking in wrong-way driving as "playing Russian roulette with their lives and everyone else’s lives". He urged parents to talk to their sons about the potential consequences if they get into a stolen car "for the craic and the clicks".

News.title: Woman ‘heartbroken’ as fiancé dies suddenly while swimming with turtles on holiday in Zante
News.content:
Woman ‘heartbroken’ as fiancé dies suddenly while swimming with turtles on holiday in Zante

EXCLUSIVE: A devastating holiday took a tragic turn when a man died suddenly just days into a trip to Greece with a friend

View 4 Images Silvana and Cameron had been together for more than 10 years

A woman has been left devastated after her fiancé died suddenly during a holiday in Greece, with his final moments coming during a trip to see turtles.

‌



Silvana Bernardes, 34, said Cameron Wallace, 33, had travelled to Zante with a friend on August 17 for a five-day break after a difficult period in his life.

‌



But just a day later, tragedy struck when Cameron entered the water during a boat trip.

‌



Silvana said she had become increasingly worried after she hadn't heard from Cameron that morning, before his friend called with the devastating news.

She said: "I woke up and for some reason I felt like something was wrong. His friend called and said, 'I don't know how to say this, something bad's happened'."

"I had a bad feeling. I just started screaming and saying 'no' and he said 'Cameron died' and I hung up the phone and just cried and sobbed."

‌



View 4 Images His cause of death remains unclear

Cameron's friend had reportedly noticed him floating unresponsive just seconds after he entered the water.

Silvana, who lives in Exeter, Devon, said: "They'd had lunch and a few drinks but nothing too much and then he went on a boat trip to find some turtles.

‌



"Within a couple of seconds of being in the water his friend noticed that he wasn't responsive and was floating next to him."

His friend performed CPR before getting him back to shore, where lifeguards took over. Cameron was then taken to hospital, but sadly died before he arrived.

Silvana said: "When he got to the hospital he was already dead. It's just terrible.

‌



"He went there to have a nice time and take his mind off things and then this terrible thing happened."

View 4 Images Silvana is now hoping Cameron can be repatriated to the UK

Cameron's death came after a worrying few months. He suffered a seizure just two days after starting a new job as a team leader at a water company on May 13.

‌



Doctors initially believed stress could have been responsible, but he was later prescribed medication after experiencing panic attacks and difficulties sleeping. He had also seen a neurologist on August 12 and was waiting for further tests.

His cause of death remains unclear, leaving Silvana desperate for answers.

She said: "We have been considering whether his death was due to the seizure. Did his heart just stop? Did he have a panic attack or a stroke?"

‌



"Whatever they rule we'll go with that just to close the chapter and move on with things."

Silvana and Cameron had been together for more than 10 years after meeting online in 2016. They became engaged in Colombia last December and had been planning to marry in Vietnam in May 2028.

View 4 Images Silvana has been left 'heartbroken'

‌



She said: "It's heartbreaking to lose him. It was so unexpected for me and his family."

Silvana is now hoping Cameron can be repatriated to the UK, with a fundraiser launched to help bring him home and support his loved ones.

She said: "It will mean a lot for me and family and friends to give him his send-off and bring him home."

‌



Paying tribute to her fiancé, she added: "There's not enough words to describe Cameron. He was a very kind man with a big heart of gold."

She said he was known for making people laugh, checking in on friends and bringing joy to those around him.

"We have been really lucky because we had some lovely holidays and travelled the world and met some lovely people. We had so many plans and so many things we wanted to happen."

Article continues below

You can donate to the fundraiser for Cameron here.

News.title: El Niño warming set to be 'strongest in living memory', warns Met Office
News.content:
The El NiÃ±o event that is developing over the Pacific Ocean is likely to be the strongest in living memory, the Met Office has warned.

The powerful natural climate phenomenon pushes up global temperatures and can increase the risks of extreme weather.

Added to the effects of human-induced climate change, the Met Office is warning that it is "very likely" to mean 2027 is the hottest year on record globally.

There is growing evidence that weather patterns around the world are already being affected, with below-average monsoon rains in India and suppressed hurricane activity in the Atlantic Ocean.

El NiÃ±o could put the UK at greater risk of a wet, stormy autumn with signs of a very unsettled spell already showing up in long-range forecasts.

"We should be clear that this is an unprecedented event," said Prof Adam Scaife, head of long-range forecasting at the UK Met Office.

"I have never seen an El NiÃ±o signal this intense in our forecasts."

There is no clear evidence that climate change is making El NiÃ±o events more likely, but its weather impacts are likely to be more extreme in a warming world.

News.title: Will Harry's return heal deep-rooted rift with William?
News.content:
This isn't a regular sibling fallout. It is a deep-rooted fracture filled with anger, resentment and a total loss of trust.

And much of it has played out in public.

The Prince of Wales remains in no mood to forgive and forget. The hurt he feels lingers.

"William is very stubborn," a family friend told the BBC. "To feel cheated by your own brother has been painful. He can't just put it behind him."

But in his interview with the BBC last year, Harry offered a different view.

"I would love reconciliation with my family. There's no point in continuing to fight any more."

The problem for Prince William now is proximity. Harry will be in the UK within two weeks, probably a short drive away from Windsor where William's family lives.

There will be pressure on the elder brother to take the lead, ease the pain and just make up with Harry now the siblings will be living in the same country.

"I think William doesn't care about the pressure to reconcile," said royal author, Valentine Low. "If he doesn't want to reconcile with his brother because of the things he's done, the wrongs that he feels Harry's done to him, he's not going to reconcile. But it does improve the chances I think."

The Prince of Wales will prioritise his public work in the coming months and try not to get drawn into the drama around the UK return of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.

Several people from organisations who have worked with Prince William told BBC News of their desire to support William and help avoid Harry and Meghan becoming a distraction.

One source, who has worked on charity projects with the Royal Family, described wanting to protect the future King.

"This is a hard situation for him full of emotion and anger and we will support him," the source said. "It is really important for me to ensure that any work we do with William will be focused on making a positive change and won't be affected by the Harry and Meghan drama."

News.title: My life was changed by a terror attack - now survivors like me won't be forgotten
News.content:
Travis Frain was texting his mates a photo he had just taken of Big Ben on a university trip to London when his day turned from normal to anything but.

"One of the guys in my group shouted 'look out' and as I looked up from my phone the terrorist's car was in front of me.

"It was a split second really before the car hit me. I went over the bonnet, into the air, before landing back on the ground."

This was 22 March 2017, when attacker Khalid Masood drove his car into crowds, killing four, before stabbing a police officer to death outside Parliament.

Frain, then 19, was left with multiple injuries including a fractured leg, which took two years to heal. "There will always be a part of you affected by that attack."

Now 28, he spoke to BBC News as the UK's first national day for victims and survivors of terrorism is set to take place on Friday.

News.title: French becoming more effective in stopping small boat crossings, UK says
News.content:
French police tactics are becoming more effective in stopping small boats in the English Channel from reaching Britain, the Home Office has said.

It credits French authorities with intercepting 185 potential crossings involving 4,300 migrants this summer over four separate weeks, as well as stopping 12 boats at sea using new techniques.

Footage released by French police shows officers racing across a beach in jeeps to intercept a launch. Once the boat is abandoned, an officer slashes it lengthways with a knife.

The Conservatives described the announcement as a "joke" and said Channel crossing preventions were "down by half over the past year".

Migrants can be seen throwing objects at the officers, one of whom appears to respond with pepper spray.

While Channel crossings are down about 40% compared to last year, thousands of illegal migrants are getting through with 250 arriving on Monday.

In late July a record 165 migrants reached the UK in a single boat with Border Security Command pictured towing a mega dinghy - estimated to be the same size as a standard bus at 13m (42ft) long - when it arrived in Dover on 23 July.

The Home Office, citing French police figures, said that since it struck a deal with France three months ago which included additional funding for authorities, 61% of small boats have been intercepted - a five per cent increase compared to last year.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the "UK-France deal is already having a real impact".

The UK-France Border Security deal agreed in April under the Starmer government, includes Â£501m over three years to strengthen operations in northern France and Â£161m for new approaches.

Previously the French authorities allowed most dinghies to head towards the UK once they had launched, because of the risk of intercepting them in deep water, while loaded with people.

Of the 12 dinghies stopped so far at sea, three interceptions took place in the last two weeks.

The techniques being used have not been disclosed by the UK or France.

Charlie Eastaugh, director of maritime and small boats at the Border Security Command, told the BBC that "last Thursday alone, the French prevented all three of the boats that tried to cross".

Speaking to the BBC at the Western Jetfoil facility in Dover used to process migrants, he said: "Two of those they prevented at sea, and one they prevented on land."

News.title: A split in the spectrum? The ongoing battle to define autism
News.content:
If someone asked you to think of an autistic person, who would come to mind?

The world's richest man, Elon Musk?

Maybe Greta Thunberg, who says being different can be a superpower.

Or Robbie Williams, who has recently revealed he's found out that he has "a bit of autism".

What about someone like 34-year old James Fitzpatrick? He doesn't talk, has a learning disability and needs constant care.

A diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) means someone has certain core characteristics including differences in how they communicate and behave. It's an umbrella term that includes people with very different experiences.

In recent years there has been an explosion in the number of people with an autism diagnosis on their GP record. In England, it has gone from just over 700,000 three years ago to around 1.1 million today.

The National Autistic Society (NAS) says "evidence suggests there is a significant underdiagnosis of autism, particularly among women and older people".

But what if some people with a diagnosis aren't actually autistic? What if they've really been misdiagnosed?

These questions largely come from 85-year-old Professor Dame Uta Frith - one of the key figures in autism research since the 1960s.

They go to the heart of a debate that is central to the identity of many autistic people.

News.title: The town whose council wants migrants to move in
News.content:
A new shop opened along Greenock's fading High Street in May. Anik African Store has brought a small corner of Nigeria to the Scottish town, selling yams, plantain, okra and catfish.

It is not the only African food shop here - there is another just metres away, responding to the area's changing population.

Five years ago, locals say, it would have been rare to see a black person in Greenock. Now hundreds of Africans and refugees have moved to the area.

The local council has in fact come up with a plan to attract even more to this corner of the west of Scotland as a means of stemming its falling population.

Scottish people "are lovely and accommodating", says Anik's owner, Christianah Omilana, who came to the UK in 2021. "Immigrants will come when there is work", she adds.

News.title: Stifling heat and broken toilets: TUI River Cruise passengers tell of their holiday hell
News.content:
Dozens of people have accused TUI River Cruises of operating vessels with faulty facilities including persistently broken air conditioning, after they spent thousands of pounds on holidays.

Earlier this year passengers on the Skyla, a ship operated by TUI, contacted BBC Your Voice to say they had been stranded in Budapest during a heatwave with little to no air conditioning.

Following that report more people got in touch to say they faced similar problems on both the Skyla and its sister vessel, the Isla. They criticised TUI's customer service and said the refunds offered were inadequate.

TUI apologised to customers where trips "fell short of the standards we aim to deliver".

A spokesperson for TUI, said: "We understand the disappointment and frustration caused to affected customers."

Passengers described stifling conditions as well as problems with plumbing after paying thousands of pounds for European cruises, including on the Danube River.

Andy Peach and his wife booked a seven-day trip on the Skyla in June, travelling through Budapest, Vienna and Linz.

It turned out to be "the worst TUI holiday we've ever been on", he said.

Instead of air conditioning, Peach said there were "big blowers" on board, expelling hot air.

"One was in the middle of the corridor, blocking the exit," he said. "It didn't seem to cool the place down."

Temperatures onboard climbed as the holiday went on leaving him "exhausted", he said. By the end of the week, Peach said the air conditioning in cabins had broken too.

On the second-to-last day passengers were transferred to hotels, which Peach said were "really basic".

He and his wife had paid nearly Â£4,000 for the holiday but they were offered only Â£300 as a refund and given 72-hours to accept it.

He said: "TUI know there's problems on these boats, but continue to sell them to people as a full luxury cruise."

News.title: UK borrows more than expected in July as Healey prepares for first Budget
News.content:
The government borrowed more than expected in July, according to figures published as Chancellor John Healey draws up his first Budget.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said borrowing, the gap between what the government spends and what it collects in tax, was Â£1.8bn during the month.

Official forecasters had expected a surplus of Â£500m, meaning the government borrowed Â£2.3bn more than predicted.

Economists warned the figure will restrict Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham's room for manoeuvre as they target measures aimed at easing the cost of living for households, with little room to increase borrowing in the Budget on 27 October.

Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" at the Budget â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

He has adopted his predecessor Rachel Reeves' fiscal rules, which commit the government to funding all day-to-day spending through tax receipts by the end of the decade.

Responding to the borrowing figures, Healey said: "We are cutting the deficit faster than any other G7 economy, while giving people a bit of breathing space with cost of living pressures and focusing support to get young people into work."

July's borrowing figure was significantly lower than June's Â£16bn, with a surge in self-assessed income tax receipts boosting the government's coffers for the month. But economists said the public finances would come under renewed pressure when the one-off lift, typical for July each year, runs out.

Despite falling from June to July, the borrowing figure was higher than expected. Experts pointed to increased welfare spending, including benefits and other payments such the state pension, with social payments coming in Â£2bn higher than the same period last year.

The ONS said borrowing from April to July, the first four months of the government's fiscal year, has reached Â£56.7bn. This is lower than last year, but Â£2.3bn higher than forecasts from the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which the government uses when drawing up its spending plans.

Senior economist at Capital Economics Ashley Webb said the figure continued a "run of bad news" for the economy and that "there will be little scope to raise borrowing in the Budget later this year".

He said the borrowing overshoot "will probably get bigger" this year as economic growth slows and the government rolls out more measures to support households with the cost of living.

Joe Nellis, head of economic research at accountancy firm MHA, also said the figures will not "prevent difficult decisions that must be made in the upcoming October Budget".

Healey will have to find "additional tax revenue, tighter control over public sector spending and changes elsewhere" to balance the books and meet the government's fiscal rules.

"Failure to do so will unsettle the financial markets and potentially push up the cost of government borrowing still further," Nellis warned.

The ONS also said Britain's overall debt pile is approaching Â£3tn, having grown by Â£127.2bn a year earlier. The Conservatives said Labour's spending would leave "ordinary families" left to cover the bill.

Shadow Chancellor Mel Stride said: "We spend more on just the interest of our soaring debt than we do on our defence, police, and prisons combined. We simply cannot afford the price of Labour."

The Liberal Democrats accused the government of pursuing an "anti-growth agenda" and called for action to lower energy bills and support high street businesses.

"In their autumn Budget, the chancellor needs to take the handbrake off Britain's economy," Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said.

The ONS also said retail sales were lacklustre in July, falling 0.5% from June. Analysts said the drop was caused by a surge of hot weather and a World Cup-induced surge in sales in June. Clothing and footwear saw the slowest growth since May last year.

News.title: Rain to stop in time for weekend as sun returns
News.content:
High pressure is set to build across the UK over the next few days bringing drier weather for the weekend.

Heavy downpours have brought rain to parts in need this week - albeit with some flash flooding - but these are set to ease.

Many areas will see sunny spells across Saturday and Sunday with daytime temperatures climbing again, perhaps to above the August average in parts of the south of England.

However the nights will turn rather chilly.

News.title: Banned driver in stolen Maserati who killed pensioner jailed
News.content:
A disqualified driver who caused the death of a great-grandfather after crashing into his garden in a stolen Maserati sports car has been jailed for 13-and-a-half years.

Fraser Garden killed 74-year-old John Bell, also known as Jack, in Broughty Ferry, near Dundee, when the crash happened in April.

The High Court in Edinburgh was told Garden, who had 90 previous convictions and two previous lifetime driving bans, had taken cocaine and was driving at almost three times the speed limit.

Judge Lord Braid told the 55-year-old that he had stolen the life of a man in what should have been the sanctuary of his own garden.

Garden previously admitted to causing Bell's death by dangerous driving.

News.title: Starmer donates biography of himself to Downing Street library
News.content:
A book about the life of Sir Keir Starmer has become the newest addition to the Downing Street library, after being donated by Sir Keir himself.

Keir Starmer: The Biography, written by journalist and former Labour adviser Tom Baldwin, has now joined the collection of more than 400 books, some of which are kept in two bookcases in Downing Street's Cabinet Room.

The library was established in 1931 by the first Labour Prime Minister, Ramsay MacDonald, and since then prime ministers and ministers have been invited to make contributions.

Seven ministers who served in Sir Keir's government have also added books to the shelves.

The new donations include:

Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves added her own book, Alice in Westminster: The political life of Alice Bacon

Darren Jones, who served as a senior minister between 2024 and 2026, gave Laudato Si: On Care for our Common Home - a book by Pope Francis which calls for greater protection of the environment

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy offered her book All In: How we build a country that works

Nick Thomas-Symonds, a Cabinet Office minister in the last government, also chose his own book - a biography of former Labour Prime Minister Harold Wilson

Women and Equalities minister Bridget Phillipson picked Choose Freedom: The Future for Democratic Socialism by former Labour deputy leader Roy Hattersley

Former Wales Secretary Jo Stevens gave The Fed: a history of the South Wales miners in the twentieth century by Hywel Francis and Davis Smith

Treasury minister James Murray donated Instruction to Deliver - a book by Sir Michael Barber about his experience being a civil servant in Tony Blair's government

As Labour leader, Sir Keir did not appear to be much of a reader. In one interview in 2024, he struggled, external to name a favourite novel and when he appeared on Radio 4's Desert Island Discs he picked an atlas as the book he would take with him.

In contrast, his successor Andy Burnham, an English Literature graduate, has spoken of his fondness for poetry, in particular the works of Tony Harrison and Philip Larkin.

He is unlikely to donate a volume to the library at this early stage of his premiership, but if he finds time to peruse the shelves, he will find an eclectic collection.

News.title: World's oldest person celebrates turning 117
News.content:
The world's oldest living person celebrates turning 117 years old in Surrey on Friday with her family and friends.

Ethel Caterham, who lives at Hallmark Lakeview Care Home in Lightwater, took on the mantle in April 2025 after the death of Brazilian nun Sister Inah Canabarro Lucas at the age of 116.

Born three years before the Titanic disaster and eight years before the Russian Revolution, Ethel has also lived through two world wars.

In addition, she is one of the oldest people to survive Covid-19, after contracting it in 2020 at the age of 110, according to Guinness World Records.

Originally from Shipton Bellinger in Hampshire, the second youngest of eight children, Ethel was raised in Tidworth, Wiltshire.

The last surviving subject of King Edward VII, as a teenager she travelled to India in 1927 and began working as an au pair to a military family there.

News.title: 'Every day is difficult' says Ashley Dale's mum four years on
News.content:
The mother of a woman shot dead by a gunman who was targeting her boyfriend has told how "every day is difficult", four years on.

Ashley Dale, 28, was murdered on 21 August 2022 when James Witham burst into her Liverpool home and began firing a Skorpion sub-machine in search of her partner, in a drugs feud.

Her mum, Julie Dale, said: "August is a difficult time for us but I just think every day is difficult."

She said it was tough to see her other two daughters reaching milestones such as leaving school and celebrating proms, adding: "You want to be happy but you're also really sad and the girls are sad their big sister's not here as well, to see their big milestones in their lives as well."

Witham was ordered to serve a minimum term of 43 years following a trial at Liverpool Crown Court.

His accomplices Niall Barry, 26, Sean Zeisz, 28, and Joseph Peers, 29, were ordered to serve prison sentences of at least 47, 42 and 41 years respectively.

News.title: 'Relentless' GCSE resit cycle 'simply not working', school and college leaders say
News.content:
The "relentless" cycle of pupils in England failing and then resitting their GCSEs in maths and English is "simply not working", a leading education union has said.

The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) said a "significant proportion" of students fall short of passing those subjects, and that most who retake those exams "face the miserable experience of falling short once again".
