Thursday's results data showed nearly one in four maths and English GCSEs in England were taken by students aged 17 and older, mostly young people resitting exams they had previously failed.

The government said it wanted to stop the "endless treadmill of unnecessary resits".

It said it would introduce a new "stepping stone" qualification from 2028 at Level 1 - one level below GCSEs - for students who do not achieve a pass in GCSE maths or English.

Currently, many courses and jobs remain dependent on students securing GCSE passes in those subjects.

But those that miss the grade can find themselves in a continuing loop of resits as they try and try again to pass.

Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of ASCL, said the fail-resit cycle was like "force feeding" students a "relentless diet of GCSE English and maths".

"This limits their education and career options and is very likely to be a factor in the large number of young people who end up not in employment, education or training," he said.

Pass rates for students aged 17 and older in English and maths are much lower than 16-year-old students taking the exams for the first time, bringing down overall GCSE grades for all ages across England, Wales and Northern Ireland as a result.

News.title: Paralympian wants to thank crash driver 44 years after accident took his leg
News.content:
A man who lost his leg after being struck by a car as a 10-year-old has said he wants to thank the driver for changing his life "for the better".

Mark Williams went on to become a world champion swimmer and won a silver medal at the 1988 Seoul Paralympics before setting up his own company.

He said the unknown driver of the car that had collided with him as he cycled home in June 1982 might now be in his 80s and could be "traumatised" by what had happened, but wanted him to know that "amazing things" had happened to him as a result.

"My biggest fear is that he doesn't know my story. I just want him to send me a message, just get in contact," he said.

Mark was 10 years old and cycling home from school on the day Prince William was born on 21 June 1982, when the crash happened.

"I had just passed my cycling proficiency. I got top marks - I was the safest rider," he said.

"I had the certificate in my rucksack, and I was riding home to show it to my mum and dad."

News.title: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemn Israel's West Bank settlement project
News.content:
Despite an Israeli court challenge to the plans by Bedouin Palestinians living in the area and Israeli peace groups, on Wednesday the Israeli housing ministry issued a tender for 1,234 of the 3,401 housing units approved by the Israeli government last August.

It covers about 12 sq km (4.6 sq miles) between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim.

At the time of their unveiling, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich - an ultranationalist and settler - said the idea of a Palestinian state was "being erased".

The deadline for bids is 19 October, just days before Israel's general election on 27 October, making it much harder for any future government to overturn any tenders issued.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

Despite the fierce international opposition, successive Israeli governments have allowed settlements to grow.

However, expansion has risen sharply since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returned to power in late 2022 at the head of a right-wing, pro-settler coalition, as well as the start of the Gaza war, triggered by Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.

Opponents of the E1 project have warned that it would effectively block the establishment of a Palestinian state because it would cut off the north of the West Bank from the south, and prevent the development in the centre of a contiguous Palestinian urban area connecting Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

News.title: 42 best beauty advent calendars for 2026 so far, reviewed as they drop
News.content:
When do beauty advent calendars usually launch?

In previous years, Liberty has kicked off the advent proceedings at the end of July, with most retailers and brands following suit into August and September. In 2026, however, a glut of beauty advent calendars dropped in July, including Harrods, Lush, Tatcha and Fortnum and Mason. The majority of other advents were subsequently revealed – in one way or another, with some brands still holding exact product rosters close to their chests – through the first week of August. As it stands, only Selfridges is left among the big four London department stores (together with Harvey Nichols , Harrods and Liberty ) to unveil its 2026 Christmas countdown.

Are beauty advent calendars worth it?

In short, yes, beauty advent calendars are always worth more than what you’ll pay; however, you have to consider whether they’ll be worth it for you personally. I’ve been diving into the best beauty advent calendars since 2015 (my first was from M&S) and I can say with confidence that some brands undoubtedly offer a better haul than others. Key things to consider are:

Do you travel a lot – Minis are part and parcel of a beauty advent calendar, so having a place to use them will be key.

Are you unsure where to start in your skincare, haircare or make-up routine – Minis can also be a great way to introduce yourself to premium brands without forking out so much initially

Do you have the time – With everything from face masks to hair bonding treatments within, these products will seriously level up your beauty regimen, but you’ll need to set aside an extra five or ten minutes to use them

What’s your budget – If you’re looking to spend less than £100, you’ll definitely have less big-name brands to choose from your haul. I recommend tallying up the cost of the products you like the look of to ensure you’re getting more than £100 of value from those formulas specifically. Extra products aren’t valuable if you won’t use them.

What is the price range of beauty advent calendars?

Beauty advent calendars can range in price from £40 to £650, with brands such as Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com ) sitting at the lower end, and luxury perfumers like Byredo in the premium price category. More typically, the core beauty advent calendars (from Boots to Harrods ) cost between £100 and £285 – though I’d argue you don’t need to spend more than £250 to take home a seriously spectacular haul.

What is the cheapest beauty advent calendar?

While there are calendars from make-up brands such as W7 (approximately £24) that offer beauty advent calendars below £30, I’d recommend looking to the likes of Revolution (£37.50, Boots.com ), Soap and Glory (£43.20, Boots.com ) and Boots x Macmillan (£44, Boots.com ) for more exciting yet affordable products.

For instance, W7 mimics packaging from Charlotte Tilbury and Estee Lauder products – to name a few – but doesn’t *actually* replicate the formula. However the Boots x Macmillan calendar boasts best-selling brands including Liz Earle and No7. After all, if your calendar costs less but you never use the products within, have you really saved money?

What was the most popular beauty advent calendar last year?

In 2025 the Space NK beauty advent calendar was arguably the most popular and sold out within a few weeks of its September launch. In fact, in previous years it was reported that two Space NK advent calendars sold every minute after its release. Following closely behind the Cult Beauty advent calendar is always a best-seller and, this year, the Harrods fragrance advent calendar has already sold out, so I’m expecting the retailer’s main beauty offering to run out of stock in the coming weeks, too.

Why you can trust IndyBest reviews

As a senior shopping writer, this will be Lucy Smith’s third year reviewing the best beauty advent calendars for IndyBest. Prior to her professional coverage, Lucy has been purchasing beauty advents from M&S, The White Company and more since 2015, putting her experience in the category at more than 10 years. Elsewhere, Lucy covers all the latest beauty launches – such as the Dyson supersonic travel dryer – year round, so she knows what the must-have products of 2026 are for this year’s advent offering. Plus, having reviewed everything from the best foundations to the best hyaluronic acid, she’s well versed in the brands that pop (and the ones that flop), so you can trust that her round-up of the best beauty advent calendars for 2026 isn’t full of hot air.

News.title: Aldi has launched a £40 cordless vacuum cleaner to rival Dyson and Shark
News.content:
Part supermarket, part budget-friendly emporium, Aldi has become the go-to store for everything from treadmills to beauty tools and more, thanks to its range of ever-changing Specialbuys that grace the middle aisle.

When it comes to nabbing home appliances at bargain prices, Aldi has you covered. One of the latest launches to catch our eye is a cordless vacuum cleaner that you can snap up for less than £40.

While premium cordless vacuums can set you back anything from a couple of hundred pounds to more than £1,000, the Ambiano (Aldi’s own-brand) cyclonic stick vacuum cleaner costs less than £40 – that’s even cheaper than our favourite tried-and-tested budget cordless vacuum cleaner.

Said to be lightweight, powerful and easy to manoeuvre, the cyclonic boasts a motorised brush with three LED lights, a 180-degree swivel head and about 32 minutes of runtime on a five-hour charge.



When can you buy Aldi’s cyclonic stick vacuum cleaner?

Aldi’s budget-friendly cordless vacuum is available in stores now. When it comes to the supermarket’s Specialbuys, stock tends to be limited and once it’s gone, it’s gone.

How much is Aldi’s cyclonic stick vacuum cleaner?

Compared with cordless vacuums from leading brands such as Dyson, Shark and Henry, Aldi’s cyclonic model costs just £39.99. It may not boast some of the premium features found on more-expensive options, but if you’re looking for a purse-friendly design for quick clean-ups, this could be an ideal choice.

Best cordless vacuum cleaners

If you miss out on Aldi’s cyclonic stick vacuum cleaner or you want something with a few more fancy features, our expert home appliances reviewer has put a range of cordless vacuums to the test. Here are a couple of her top picks.

Henry quick pro “The quick pro was the best cordless vacuum in our tests, as it’s ideal for daily use,” said reviewer Joanne Lewsley. It boasts a 60-minute runtime and LED lights for spotting crumbs under furniture. Joanne was impressed with the suction power, describing it as “excellent on hard floors and carpets”. She added that the “swivel steering made it surprisingly nimble”, too. Read Joanne’s full review of the Henry quick pro. £399 £249 from Currys.co.uk Prices may vary

Akitas cordless vacuum cleaner If you don’t manage to get your hands on Aldi’s cordless vacuum, appliances reviewer Joanne Lewsley rates this model from Akitas, which is currently available for just £10 more than Aldi’s cyclonic design. “It proved itself to be a handy, budget-friendly option that’s well-suited to everyday vacuuming on hard floors,” said Joanne, after putting it to the test in her own home. While Joanne added that the suction power isn’t especially powerful, compared with premium models, she described it as “a no-frills cleaner that gets the job done on a budget”. Read Joanne’s full review of the Akitas cordless vacuum cleaner. £60 £50 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary

For more recommendations, check out our review of the best carpet cleaners

Royal Mail has missed its delivery targets once again but said it was making progress to meet the goals as it rolls out a major overhaul to scrap second-class post on Saturdays.

The group said it delivered 85% of first-class deliveries the next day and 91.4% of second-class mail within three working days during the first quarter of the year.

Under targets set by Ofcom, 90% of first-class mail should be delivered the next day, and 95% of second-class mail should be delivered within three days.

From April 1, the watchdog lowered previous delivery targets for first-class from 93% and second-class from 98.5% as part of universal service reforms.

open image in gallery Royal Mail expects to complete the rollout of the new model across all its 1,200 delivery offices by Christmas (PA) ( PA Archive )

But Royal Mail insisted it had seen a marked improvement from a year earlier, when first quarter figures showed just 76% of first-class and 89.3% of second-class post arrived on time.

The group – whose owner International Distribution Services was bought last year by Czech billionaire Daniel Kretinsky – recently pledged to meet the Ofcom delivery targets by May 2027 as part of a plan to invest £500 million in the service over the next five years.

Last July, Ofcom gave postal reforms the green light to reflect steep declines in the number of letters being sent, allowing second-class letters to be delivered on alternate weekdays only.

Royal Mail expects to complete the rollout of the new model across all its 1,200 delivery offices by Christmas, after initially being delayed until it had reached agreement with trade unions.

Jamie Stephenson, Royal Mail chief operating officer, said: “These results are encouraging and show that the work we are doing to improve the service is having an impact.

“First-class performance is well ahead of where we expected to be at this stage of our improvement plan, while second-class is tracking in line with the plan.”

But he said “we know there is more to do”.

Ofcom launched an investigation in June into Royal Mail’s failure to meet its delivery targets for the second year running in the 12 months to the end of March.

Police in India’s capital of Delhi busted a multi-city racket trafficking counterfeit and illegally diverted anti-cancer drugs, arrested 17 people, and seized medicines worth Rs 90m (£688,188) in a major crackdown.

The syndicate, involving hospital and nursing staff, allegedly traded in stolen and fake cancer treatment drugs from several government hospitals while replacing some of those with counterfeit medicines.

The alleged network operated across Delhi and national capital region, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and other locations.

Police said the drugs were sourced through three channels.

The first was the diversion of medicines from government institutions and warehouses, the second through theft of medicines, vials and packaging material from private hospitals, and the last through the manufacturing of counterfeit medicines.

“The accused themselves made counterfeit drugs by imitating the vials and the packing and using fake batch numbers. They filled them with sterilised water and sold them as real drugs to desperate patients at discounted prices,” a senior police officer said, according to The Indian Express.

The drugs seized included immunotherapy medicines and drugs used in targeted therapies, including Darzalex, Imfinzi, Erbitux, Opdyta, Gazyva, Bavencio, Adcetris and Keytruda.

At least 17 arrested from across India for allegedly running a massive fake cancer treatment drug racket ( @CrimeBranchDP )

The cost of these life-saving medicines for cancer patients ranges from Rs 15,000 (£114) to Rs 200,000 (£1530) per vial or injection.

Aditya Gautam, deputy commissioner of police, Crime Branch, said 588 filled anti-cancer vials, six empty vials, seven empty medicine boxes and 3,021 units of other medicines, worth up to Rs 90m, were recovered. Around Rs 5,000,000 (£38,000 approx) in cash was also recovered.

The investigation began on 22 June after the Crime Branch received information about the racket. Following verification, police identified suspicious premises in East Delhi, Rohini and Mumbai.

Seven teams conducted simultaneous raids in Delhi and Navi Mumbai on 11 July in coordination with the drugs department and local police. Further arrests followed interrogations and searches, police said.

“The medicines were procured without valid invoices, purchase records, drug licences or other required documentation and stored at residential and other premises before being circulated through intermediaries,” Mr Gautam said.

Police said batch numbers, maximum retail prices and other identifying marks were allegedly removed using chemicals including acetone to conceal the source and identity of the medicines during the repackaging process.

Packaging material such as thermocol boxes, bubble wrap, adhesive tape and polythene was also recovered, along with registers and diaries allegedly recording medicine and cash transactions.

The latest crackdown is another blow to India’s reputation as the “pharmacy of the world”, a description prime minister Narendra Modi has himself used to highlight the country’s growing pharmaceutical reach.

In 2026, the government has said India is seeking to move from being the “pharmacy of the world” to a global innovation hub, with quality and reliability central to that ambition.

India is also a hub for international patients arriving for cheaper treatment.

Government data shows that 507,244 foreign nationals travelled to India for medical treatment in 2025, with cancer treatment among the specialised procedures sought by international patients.

Police said Anand Kumar, a former pharmaceutical firm operator, was allegedly a key intermediary, with 337 anti-cancer vials recovered from him. Police also alleged that several accused used pharmaceutical businesses and invoices to facilitate the movement of medicines.

Jaswant Sharma, a nursing-qualified oncology department in-charge, allegedly removed medicines from a hospital, while Manish Sharma, another nursing-qualified worker, allegedly misappropriated injections, police said.

Police also alleged that Deepak alias Ravi, a dental technician and former personal assistant to an oncologist, received vials from nursing staff. Officers said 108 vials were recovered from him.

India is the world's third-largest producer of drugs and pharmaceuticals by volume, accounting for about 10 per cent of total production by volume.

However, high-profile incidents, including the deaths of children in The Gambia and India linked to contaminated Indian-made cough syrups, have sparked global warnings from the WHO over tainted products. India-made cough syrups were linked to the deaths of more than 140 children in Africa and Central Asia, and 24 children in central India.

Five people are missing after a huge fire tore through a residential block housing a restaurant and apartments in a Swiss Alpine town.

Eight others were injured in the blaze, which broke out in Thusis, a part of the eastern canton of Graubünden, which attracts visitors throughout the year for its Alpine scenery.

The fire broke out just after midnight, where emergency services were alerted at around 00:00 local time on Friday, according to the local police service.

The severity of the blaze saw almost 100 firefighters from various local networks rush to the scene.

open image in gallery Five people have been reported as missing after the outbreak of the fire ( Kantonspolizei Graubunden )

Fourteen people managed to escape the burning building, the Graubünden Cantonal police said.

Two of those who escaped suffered serious injuries, while two others were moderately injured and a further four sustained minor injuries.

The injured were taken to hospitals in Chur, Thusis, Ilanz and Zurich.

open image in gallery Large amounts of smoke were seen rising from the residential complex ( Kantonspolizei Graubunden )

Firefighters faced difficult conditions inside the building after the stairwell collapsed, with police stating that the building had been “completely destroyed” by the blaze.

The collapse of the stairwell made access to parts of the property more difficult as emergency crews worked to bring the fire under control.

Because of this, the roof of the block had to be opened using a crane to tackle the flames from above.

open image in gallery A crane was used to lift off the roof of the building and quell the blaze ( Kantonspolizei Graubunden )

Specialist teams are working through the heavily damaged structure as the search continues for the missing.

Authorities have not said whether they believe those missing were inside the building when the fire broke out.

While initial findings indicate the blaze began on the second floor, investigators have not yet established what caused it.

Police and prosecutors have launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fire.

In a separate incident late on Thursday morning a fire broke out in the kitchen of an apartment in a building in the northern city of Schaffhausen.

“Eleven people were injured, nine of whom have been taken to hospital,” local police said. They added that a police officer was among the injured.

TikTok creator @fashionableforecast even described it, alongside the liner and lipstick hue, as "possibly the most unwearable shades I've ever seen.” While I’m not sure I agree entirely, another red lipstick does feel ever so slightly uninspiring.

As of today (21 August), with four new formulas to get excited about, Cult Beauty seems to have clawed back favour, especially with the latest high-value full-size products in the mix. Namely, Allies of Skin azelaic & kojic advanced clarifying serum (worth £94), Sulwhasoo first care activating serum (worth £45) and, to satisfy Korean skincare lovers, Anua PDRN hyaluronic acid 100 moisturising cream (worth £24). Though, only time will tell whether the products behind the remaining nine doors prove as equally wow-worthy.

Beyond those first reveals, Cult Beauty has promised 12 launches from the past 12 months, meaning there should still be plenty of fresh discoveries to come. As a beauty writer, I'm hoping that includes recent innovations such as K18's futureIQ biomimetic hair longevity serum and the new Color Wow money laundering shampoo and conditioner.

As for the remains of what we do know, Cult Beauty fans are set to receive "more customer favourite brands than ever", which, when you browse the retailer's trending section, could point to the likes of Vieve, Medik8, Gisou and more. We also know that those buying the calendar will have the chance to win one of three £1,000 Cult Beauty vouchers and that there will be a total 17 full-size products. Unfortunately, this is a three-product decrease year on year, despite a £5 increase in price. I'm holding off on judging that just yet, though, because Cult Beauty has a knack for thoughtful curation, and there's every chance the smaller line-up will be offset by stronger product choices.

The retailer always delights fans with a unique calendar design, and this year it's been created in collaboration with Swindler & Swindler, whose Victorian-inspired botanical illustrations feel elegant rather than overtly festive.

The waitlist for the 2026 advent calendar is now live, and this is one sign-up you don't want to skip. Not only will you'll get priority access before the general sale, but you'll also receive a £20 Cult Beauty gift card to redeem when purchasing on launch day.

Stay tuned for all the latest updates as they come in. I'll be keeping this guide updated with every new product reveal, launch detail and spoiler as soon as it's announced.

A Canadian provincial premier launched a sharp attack on President Donald Trump on Thursday, calling him a "bad person" and "not to be trusted" while urging Canada to keep fighting rather than rush trade concessions with Washington.

Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew said Canada holds leverage in talks even as his province considers restoring U.S. alcohol sales at Prime Minister Mark Carney’s request to avert threatened 50% U.S. tariffs.

Kinew also predicted that Trump would be “slaughtered” in the midterm elections.

open image in gallery Premier of Manitoba Wab Kinew listens to questions during a press conference at Canada's Premier's Conference in Toronto in 2024 ( AFP/Getty )

"Everybody knows the American president by now, he’s erratic, he’s irresponsible, and he’s not to be trusted. And this is the person that we were supposed to make a deal with, and we’re going to make additional concessions for it. That’s why I say you can't make a good deal with a bad person, because who’s to say it’s not going to be undone?" Kinew said.

Dominic LeBlanc, the federal minister responsible for Canada-U.S. trade, said Thursday both nations are nearing a final agreement after returning to Washington to meet U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

"We’re very close. We continue to make progress," he said, adding Canadian officials will remain in Washington working on the deal. Trump called the agreement "very fair" to both sides, while tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian imports are delayed until 12::green-background[01] a.m. Saturday. Full terms remain unreleased.

open image in gallery Despite his criticism of Trump, Kinew said Manitoba may go along with Carney’s request as part of a “Team Canada” approach ( Getty )

Despite criticizing Trump, Kinew said Manitoba might join Carney’s "Team Canada" approach, though he urged consumers to buy Canadian if U.S. products return to shelves. Other provincial leaders, including the premiers of Saskatchewan and Nova Scotia, publicly backed Carney’s negotiating direction.

Newfoundland and Labrador Premier Tony Wakeham said all premiers agreed during a Wednesday call with Carney to restock U.S. alcohol, though not all have publicly confirmed that position.

"I think we should fight. I think Donald Trump is very weak. I think America is weaker around the world today than it was a year ago. He’s about to get slaughtered in the midterms and the cost of living is the number one issue and he’s completely out of touch with the cost of living of Americans," Kinew said.

open image in gallery Eight of Canada’s 10 provinces restrict or ban U.S. alcohol — measures imposed in retaliation for Trump’s previous tariffs on Canadian goods ( Reuters )

"We’ve got the upper hand. They are back on their heels right now. They are coming to us for a deal right now."

Reinstating alcohol sales remains a key sticking point.

Kinew said he understood Carney’s request meant restoring U.S. alcohol sales was essential to complete the deal. Provincial bans have annoyed the Trump administration, which pressed Canada to lift restrictions that severely reduced American liquor sales.

Provincial governments lack veto power over the broader Canada-U.S. agreement, but control liquor sales and procurement rules involved in negotiations.

open image in gallery Grafitti calling for a boycott on American wine at a liquor store in Montreal, Canada ( AFP/Getty )

Eight of Canada’s 10 provinces restrict U.S. alcohol—measures imposed over Trump’s previous tariffs and his comments about making Canada the 51st U.S. state.

Kinew said Carney pressed premiers to restore U.S. alcohol sales while other details were finalized. "I wouldn’t say that he was begging us, but what is the step before begging?" Kinew said.

Ontario, Canada’s most populous province, is crucial. Its government-run LCBO, among the world's largest alcohol buyers, imported nearly 1 billion Canadian dollars ($723 million) in U.S. products annually before pulling them last year.

open image in gallery Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who previously clashed with Trump, has not commented on the deal ( AFP/Getty )

Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who previously clashed with Trump, has not commented on the deal.

Kinew said Canadians should avoid American goods even if returned.

"When we put the American booze back on the Liquor Mart shelves, Canadians, leave it there. Spend your money on Canadian products that are going to employ people in our country and that have an administration that respects Canada," Kinew said.

Kinew said Manitoba could remove formal restrictions on U.S. companies and products, including procurement preferences, while still favoring Canadian suppliers in provincial purchasing.

Preferring to keep fighting, Kinew noted the U.S. Republican president’s habit of levying heavy tariffs before retreating. He cited the "TACO" acronym coined by Financial Times writer Robert Armstrong: "Trump Always Chickens Out."

"Do we expect that this is going to be the end of Donald Trump?," Kinew said.

Meanwhile, Quebec Premier Christine Fréchette said Carney answered many questions about the agreement, though she withheld endorsement while assessing its economic impact. She said Quebec could restore U.S. alcohol at the SAQ, the state enterprise controlling provincial liquor sales, but stressed the decision remains Quebec’s.

Robert Bothwell, a professor emeritus of Canadian history and international relations at the University of Toronto, said Kinew’s comments reflect widespread Canadian sentiment. "Kinew speaks for Canada," Bothwell said. "The majority of the Canadian people hates Trump."

The recent heatwaves mean that many people in northern Europe are now looking at new ways to cool their homes.

Historically, northern European building design has prioritised heating, but more homeowners are considering adding air conditioning.

While 88% of US homes have air conditioning, only about 3% of UK homes have it.

What are the big issues?

Fitting an air-conditioning system to an existing home is likely to cost more than £6,000 for a whole house. It will also mean running pipework through walls, which may require renovation afterwards. Running costs range from a few hundred pounds to a few thousand per year depending on the size of the UK property. It is worth remembering that electricity in the UK is twice the cost of the US, where more homes have air conditioning.

Typically, to fit air conditioning, you have an outdoor unit (the condenser) and a fan unit mounted on the wall or in the ceiling, connected by pipes. These pipes feed cold water from the condenser into the fan unit, which cools the air (which can be reversed in winter to provide heating). This is known as a split system.

Fitting an air-conditioning system to an existing home is likely to cost more than £6,000 for a whole house ( Alamy/PA )

Then there’s planning and consent. Condensers generate noise and can be unsightly. You generally don’t need planning permission if units are discreetly located. But this is difficult to do with flats, as the units create noise which may disturb nearby properties. Planning consent is likely to be required, so it’s worth checking. Air conditioning must also comply with various building regulations, for instance those related to safety.

Adding to historic homes

Another factor is the age and construction of the existing home. Historic buildings have thick stone walls and a large thermal mass, so they take longer to cool down or heat up. Often, they are deliberately designed to be airy and well ventilated, as this helps control problems like high humidity. However, this means a higher rate of air leakage, so air conditioning units have to work harder. Plus those high ceilings means a larger air volume to cool. Installation may also require special planning permission and may be more complex and expensive.

It is also worth considering the levels of humidity. This may rise depending on the air conditioning system used, and could be a particular problem in historic buildings. When air temperature drops, as happens if you cool it, the humidity inside a room increases. This may mean a dehumidifier is needed.

About the author Dylan Ryan is a Lecturer in Mechanical & Energy Engineering at Edinburgh Napier University. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Another air conditioning option is to use portable units. These combine everything in a single machine. However, they are only intended to cool small spaces and would tend to be less energy efficient, with higher running costs. They also need a duct to dump the heat, which typically means fitting a vent to an outside wall or window. Sticking the pipe out of an open window will let the heat in and the chilled air escape. Installing US-style window units may require a chat with a planning department first to check on restrictions. These also need windows that open vertically (such as sash windows), which isn’t typical in many modern UK homes.

When shopping for air conditioning, much like “miracle” heater scams, also be wary of similar scams regarding “miracle” coolers at cheap prices.

Environmental consequences

Environmental impact has long been another concern. Historically air conditioning used ozone-eating CFCs as a refrigerant, but these are no longer used in units on sale today. Air conditioners still do contribute to the urban heat island effect, which makes cities hotter, as the heat from the building is released via the condenser into the surrounding air. This heat island effect is likely to be a factor in making heatwaves worse.

Carbon emissions will vary, depending on the source of electricity. In France or Portugal, where the grid is nearly all carbon neutral (nuclear, hydro, solar or wind), emissions would be low. But they’d be much higher in Poland or Cyprus, for instance, which use relatively few renewables and limited or no nuclear sources in their national electricity mixes.

Other options?

Given that heat pumps are increasingly standard in new UK homes, configuring them to also provide cooling in the summer could become the way forward. Most existing UK systems are not set up to do this, but more are likely to go on sale if demand rises.

Another option that will save on your energy bills is to try to cope with summer heat using what is called passive cooling, by adding awnings, external shutters or shading your windows. These are definitely the lowest cost options and can be easiest to install, and should bring the temperature down. This is traditionally how buildings were kept cool in summer.

Heatwaves are part of the cost of climate change. And while weighing up the ways to cope with it, it’s also vital to think about how our choices could also escalate the continuing extreme weather, particularly given that it will affect older and more vulnerable people more adversely.

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

CRYSENCIO SUMMERVILLE fumbled the chance to open his Al-Hilal account as his cheeky panenka went horribly wrong.

The £60million summer signing from West Ham was handed the chance to convert from 12 yards after the Saudi side were awarded a penalty while 2-0 up at Al-Fayha on Thursday night.



He took a deep breath and disguised his chipped attempt, with the keeper diving down to his right.

But Summerville overcooked the dink and, to his horror, the ball clipped the top of the crossbar and flew behind.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

The Dutchman, 24, put his head in his hands and wiped his face with his jersey.

All the while he was getting a rollicking from team-mate Sergej Milinkovic-Savic, who was seen shouting and gesturing in his direction.



Summerville was subbed off four minutes later before Nasser Al Dawsari rounded off a comfortable 3-0 win in the 88th minute.

It has been a tough start for Summerville in Saudi, failing to contribute to any of the seven goals Al-Hilal have netted in his two appearances thus far.

The Saudi giants’ squad also includes Karim Benzema, Darwin Nunez, Joao Cancelo, Theo Hernandez, Kalidou Koulibaly and Ruben Neves.

Sports.title: EFL club’s former 8,300-capacity stadium now a building site as demolition begins and stand is destroyed
Sports.content:
ROTHERHAM UNITED’S old home is being RIPPED apart as demolition work gets under way at Millmoor.

The former 8,300-capacity stadium is now a building site, a whole 18 years after the Millers left.



Drone footage released by the BBC shows diggers tearing through the Main Stand with huge sections of terracing already destroyed.

While the roof and steel frame look to still be in place, the whole thing is set to be dragged down as the historic ground disappears piece by piece.





Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

Rotherham played at Millmoor from 1907 until 2008, when an ownership row forced them to pack up their things.

They moved six miles away to Don Valley Stadium in Sheffield for four years before returning to the town in 2012.

But the Millers have played at the purpose-built 12,000-capacity New York Stadium – just a stone’s throw from their old ground – ever since.

Millmoor has remained frozen in time, with the pitch, goalposts and crumbling stands still in place.



Work on a new Main Stand started in around 2005 but ground to a halt two years later and was never completed.

Sports.title: Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed
Sports.content:
Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed

Reigning champions Arsenal get their Premier League season underway tonight against Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium - but Mikel Arteta has a new fitness doubt

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Frank Lampard go head-to-head this evening as Arsenal host Coventry (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Mikel Arteta is sweating on the fitness of Bruno Guimaraes heading into tonight’s game against Coventry City. Arsenal begin the defence of their Premier League title against Frank Lampard’s side at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Guimaraes, who joined the Gunners from Newcastle United earlier this month, was forced off during the Community Shield victory over Manchester City last weekend. And speaking on Thursday afternoon, Arteta admitted: "Let's see how it is, it's evolving well, but let's see for tomorrow."

‌



However, Arteta will be without defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber. Saliba is continuing his rehabilitation from a back injury sustained at the World Cup, while Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

‌



“No, I said in the next few weeks,” Arteta said on Thursday when asked if Timber can join team training this week. “He's not training with the group yet.”

But there was better news for Gunners supporters, with Arteta confirming that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are fit to start against the Sky Blues. The Arsenal boss said: “Yes, they're ready to be involved, yes.”

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas READ MORE :

While Frank Lampard confirmed on Thursday that Coventry will be without striker Haji Wright for the games against the Gunners. Wright was Coventry’s top scorer last season, scoring 17 times as his side won the Sky Bet Championship.

‌



The striker has been absent from recent friendly matches against RCD Espanyol and AS Monaco. And Lampard admitted his star man could be out for as long as 12 weeks. He said: “Haji Wright won’t be available for the Arsenal game.

“He won’t be available for a little while, he’s got a very serious quad injury which is disappointing for Haji and for us. It’s certainly going to be a number of weeks, could even be up to 12 weeks.”

Lampard, though, did confirm that both Ephron Mason-Clark and Jack Rudoni will be in contention to feature at the Emirates after they missed games in pre-season.

‌



View 2 Images Haji Wright won't be available for Coventry City (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Coventry boss also admitted his side need to be ready for “tougher times” this season ahead of their Premier League curtain-raiser. He said: “We will go through tougher times this year for sure because of the competition we’re up against now so we’ll need resilience in moments calmness in moments.

‌



“An important part of my role is to have that balance and through having a long playing career through having a managerial career where I’ve had some really great moments and some difficult moments.

“But as a club we will need to stick together in those moments but I want to sound like I’m being too negative before something’s happened. It’s just a reality that we need to be ready for.

“Second spell at Chelsea wasn’t great for me, for a PR point. But having been through the challenges for good and for bad in my managerial career I think it puts me in a better spot to deal with – don’t get too high, don’t get too low – continue and focus on your.”

Sports.title: Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark
Sports.content:
Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark

Tottenham have spent heavily so far this summer following a dismal campaign and Roberto De Zerbi’s men are now set to raid Manchester City for two big-money signings

View 2 Images Spurs have agreed a deal to sign Savinho (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham have agreed a deal worth up to £85m to sign Manchester City winger Savinho. The North London side are long-term admirers of the Brazilian winger, having failed to agree terms on a €50million (£43.3m) deal last summer.

‌



But they have retained their interest in the 22-year-old and are now close to finally securing his services. According to The Athletic, Spurs have agreed to pay £75m up-front for the former Troyes man, with £10m in potential bonuses.

‌



Should the deal go through as expected, it would represent a record sale for City, eclipsing the £81m sale of Julian Alvarez to Atletico Madrid in 2024.

‌



Savinho would also become the latest high-profile departure from the Etihad Stadium this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Nathan Ake, Bernardo Silva and John Stones having all left alongside former boss Pep Guardiola.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sales might not even be finished there, either. Spurs are also in talks with City over a deal for Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush.

‌



A deal for both him and Savinho is expected to cost around £140m - meaning Marmoush is valued at around £55m. The 27-year-old only joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt in January last year and has gone on to net 16 goals in 62 appearances.

Meanwhile, Savinho joined the club from French side Troyes in 2024 but has only netted twice in 53 Premier League outings.

Once their moves to North London are complete, they will become the latest arrivals in what has been an astonishing £369m rebuild under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs have already signed Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke for big fees, while Marcos Senesi, Andrew Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all joined on free transfers.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Marmoush is expected to follow Savinho to North London (Image: Getty Images)

Spurs start their season against London rivals Brentford on Saturday evening, while Man City entertain Bournemouth on Sunday. Ahead of that game, City boss Enzo Maresca has already hinted that more signings could arrive before the deadline.

He said: "We knew already before the game the things that we need to do. It is not because we lost the game. We are quite clear. For sure, we are going to do something before the transfer window closes."

Article continues below

City have been linked with Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi but the Italian remained tight-lipped on a deal. He added: "He is still a Lille player. But any new signing as soon as they arrive, it’s better [for us], because we have the Premier League starting in one week."

Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Virgil van Dijk makes 'unacceptable' claim as club approve three transfer exits

Liverpool are just days away from their Premier League opener against Newcastle United but the transfer window is still wide open

View 3 Images Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola is all set for his debut Premier League season at Anfield (Image: Getty)

Liverpool's Premier League curtain-raiser against Newcastle United is just around the corner. But Andoni Iraola's squad have only welcomed three new additions so far this summer.

‌



In his first season in charge, new manager Iraola, who has supplanted Arne Slot, will travel to St. James' Park on Sunday. But clubs have until September 1 to conclude their transfer business.

‌



Victor Munoz (£34.6million), Jeremy Jacquet (£60m) and Ronald Araujo (loan with a £47.1m purchase option) complete the Reds' incomings. But with Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson departing, some feel there is still a lot to be done.

‌



However, another exit has been confirmed and two more are on the cards as Mirror Football brings you all the latest transfer updates from Anfield.

Reds allow three to leave

Liverpool have allowed young attacker Kieran Morrison to join Sheffield Wednesday on loan for the 2026/27 season. He will be followed out of the door by Calvin Ramsay and Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

‌



View 3 Images Morrison has joined Sheffield Wednesday (Image: Getty)

‌



Now, reports suggest he is all set to sign for St. Mirren on loan. He is out of contract next summer, meaning his Reds career could effectively be over. Ndukwe, the final departing star, impressed hugely in pre-season.

However, work permit issues mean the 18-year-old centre-back cannot play senior football yet for the Reds. Therefore, he is being shipped out on loan to Spanish side Levante and he has jetted in ahead of a move to La Liga, where he will play until at least January.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Michael Carrick to get transfer gift as medical booked for double deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick to get transfer gift as medical booked for double deal

Manchester United are reportedly involved in several transfer dealings as Michael Carrick looks to improve his squad ahead of the new Premier League season

View 3 Images Manchester United manager Michael Carrick will guide his team into the new campaign (Image: Getty)

Manchester United are set for a busy end to the summer transfer window. Manager Michael Carrick remains focused on strengthening his squad ahead of deadline day on September 1.

‌



United have submitted a bid worth up to £65m for Brighton star Carlos Baleba as part of the club's midfield overhaul. He would become the third midfielder to head to Old Trafford this summer, after the completion of moves for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

‌



The 22-year-old midfielder would become the team's most expensive signing of the window so far. However, Carrick's side are set to recoup some of their transfer outlay through a sell-on clause which is expected to be activated this summer.

‌



Meanwhile, the Red Devils look set to lose out on two academy prospects to Arsenal. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest transfer stories surrounding United.

Michael Carrick to get transfer gift

United are set to receive an unexpected gift in the transfer window, with former defender Willy Kambwala all set to leave Villarreal. The 21-year-old made 10 appearances for United before joining the Spanish club in 2024.

‌



View 3 Images Kambwala left United in 2024 (Image: Getty)

The Manchester Evening News reports that United included a "sizeable" sell-on fee when dealing with Villarreal two years ago. Italian club Como are claimed to be leading the race for Kambwala's signature, while La Liga club Osasuna have also shown interest.

The situation means United will receive a small sum when Kambwala leaves Villarreal, as he is not expected to command a significant fee, which reduces the amount heading back to Old Trafford. Sports.title: Atletico Madrid 'agree to sell Julian Alvarez to Arsenal' - but there's a catch
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid 'agree to sell Julian Alvarez to Arsenal' - but there's a catch

Julian Alvarez issued a public transfer request at the World Cup and Atletico Madrid appear to have finally accepted that selling him is now the only viable solution

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez wants to leave Atletico Madrid (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Atletico Madrid have finally changed their stance and are now open to selling Julian Alvarez to Arsenal - but the player remains steadfast in his desire to join Barcelona instead.

‌



Alvarez, 26, is desperate to join Barca, who saw their €100million (£86m) bid rejected earlier this summer and were the subject of a complaint to FIFA from Atletico for allegedly tapping the player up.

‌



That was the after Alvarez went public with his desire to leave during the World Cup. Atletico boss Diego Simeone declared earlier this month that the Argentina international's future had been decided, with the striker set to remain in Madrid for another season.

‌



But Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo report that the situation has become untenable, forcing Atletico to accept a sale - except not to Barcelona. Simeone would even accept taking Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres as part of a swap deal which has been mooted in recent weeks.

Alvarez, however, doesn't want to return to England, having chosen to leave Manchester City in 2024. His heart is set on joining Barcelona, which is believed to be his 'dream' club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

In June, Alvarez declared: "I spoke with people at the club, with those I had to speak with and the best thing for everyone is ‌a transfer and I want to fulfil my dream. It's not the time to talk about this, but I also can't hide ⁠it. I try to ⁠be an honest person."

CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin has been firm, though, claiming that the only way in which Alvarez can be sold is if a club pays his extravagant €500million (£428m) release clause. "We don't want to transfer him," Gil Marin stated.

‌



"We didn't accept the €100m offer, nor will we accept one for €150m or €200m. I have no doubt that Atletico is the right place for Julian and that Julian is the centre forward for Atletico Madrid. We want to keep him."

Should Julian Alvarez join Arsenal? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez didn't play in Atletico Madrid's opener (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



Alvarez missed Atletico's first game of the La Liga season, a 2-0 win at home to Malaga. Simeone explained pre-match that the former City star wasn't match fit, having been granted extra time off after helping Argentina reach the World Cup final.

"We don't believe Julian Alvarez is in the right condition to play or take part for tomorrow's game," the Atletico boss said. "Hopefully, over these next four days, he'll make further progress and we'll be closer to where we want him to be.

"We're looking after both the person and the player, and we understand that he is not in the right condition to play in this match."

Article continues below

Atletico's next game is on Sunday, hosting Villarreal. It remains to be seen whether Alvarez will feature.

Sports.title: Michael Owen burst out crying with son's heartbreaking diagnosis 'a ticking time bomb'
Sports.content:
Michael Owen burst out crying with son's heartbreaking diagnosis 'a ticking time bomb'

Liverpool, Manchester United and England icon Michael Owen has opened up on his son's health in a new tell-all Amazon series

View 3 Images Michael Owen opens up on his personal life in the new documentary (Image: Prime Video)

Former England hero Michael Owen has opened up on his son’s “ticking time bomb” eye condition. Michael’s son, James, 20, has Stargardt, which is a rare eye disorder.

‌



The disease is inherited and causes progressive central vision loss. This usually begins in childhood or adolescence and can lead to blurry, hazy, or distorted vision.

‌



Michael, who played for Liverpool, Newcastle and Manchester United in the Premier League, admits to breaking down in tears upon learning that his son had Stargardt in his new reality series, ‘Meet the Owens’, which premieres on Amazon this week. The show gives insight into the private lives of Michael, his wife Louise, and their four children, Gemma, James, Emily, and Jessica.

‌



Talking in the show, the Liverpool icon says: “When he first got diagnosed, I remember stopping in the car, three or four times, and just bursting out crying, thinking, ‘What’s his life going to be like?’ I just wanted him to not feel sorry for himself, wanted him to have a positive outlook on life.”

James states that the condition is “like a ticking timebomb,” adding that he could go fully blind in the future. Michael also touches upon the pain and guilt he feels about James being unable to follow him into football, due to his health issues.

Arsenal dynasty predicted as one promoted team backed to survive Premier League READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola faces Liverpool problem Arne Slot couldn't solve as tactics take their toll READ MORE :

He adds: "Most people who play football have the dream of their son following in their footsteps. That’s what my dad had with me. I wanted James to be a footballer when he was really young but obviously that dream was dashed quite early.

‌



“We made James, and I don’t think I’d be normal if I didn’t put myself in the mirror and think, 'It’s down to us that he’s got this eye condition” so I did feel guilty for a little while and could say I still feel guilty now, but you look at the positives with him and the guilt sort of evaporates."

View 3 Images Michael Owen has opened up about James' health (Image: BBC)

Away from his family, Meet the Owens gives fans an unfiltered insight into Michael himself. Ultimately, his great passion is Manor House Stables, where he and his staff train and race horses.

‌



In the show, Owen says he has put “£13million to £14million” into the stables as he looks to make it one of the most successful in the industry.

However, the ex-forward knows the pitfalls of the business and at one point admits that he “can’t keep haemorrhaging” money. In one scene, he tells wife Louise: “So we bought three horses today…..£273,000 we spent. Over a quarter of a million. Let’s just hang off on that new kitchen you wanted?”

‌



Michael also discusses his reputation for being, as he says in the show, “a boring p***k”, adding: “Even my kids say, 'Dad, everyone sees you as dead boring.”

However, he hits out at those who have made fun of some of his more viral moments in the past. Speaking to Simon Jordan on the latter’s Up Front podcast in December 2023, Owen discussed how competitive he was from an early age.

View 3 Images Michael Owen shows his funny side in the new show (Image: Amazon)

‌



On that podcast he said: “Everything was a challenge. I’d eat an apple watching the TV at night and the bin would be by the TV about six metres away. And I had the bravery to [throw the apple] and miss and for there to be a stain on the wallpaper. My mum would absolutely scream at me and send me upstairs."

Sports.title: Liverpool 'need five more signings' with three transfer targets absolute musts
Sports.content:
Liverpool 'need five more signings' with three transfer targets absolute musts

Liverpool have made three senior signings this summer but Andoni Iroala has been told he must bring in some more reinforcements

View 2 Images Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has been told to strengthen his squad (Image: Getty)

Liverpool legend Phil Thompson believes the club still need up to five new signings and has named three positions that the Reds must prioritise. Andoni Iraola is set for his first season at Anfield, but Thompson has expressed doubts about the squad's ability to challenge for the Premier League title.

‌



The 72-year-old particularly worries about the defensive options at Iraola's disposal ahead of Liverpool's opening game against Newcastle. Centre-back Ibrahima Konate and experienced full-back Andy Robertson have both left at the end of their contracts.

‌



Jeremy Jacquet has subsequently arrived from Rennes, while Barcelona's Ronald Araujo has joined on loan for the season to bolster the club's back-line. However, former defender Thompson is adamant that up to five new players are needed, specifically name-checking the defence, midfield and out wide as areas to strengthen.

‌



Speaking on the Footy Accumulators No Tippy Tappy Football podcast, in partnership with BOYLE Sports, he said: "Defensively, we do need more. It is a particular area if Jacquet isn't fully ready, who is going to be there? It's a difficult one. We still need recruitment.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Virgil van Dijk sends clear message to Liverpool owners for final days of transfer window READ MORE :

"I think we probably need four, maybe five players in total in different positions. Defensively, certainly, a midfield player, a wide player; you need two quality players for every position. There's work to be done."

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool legend Thompson has made his thoughts clear (Image: Getty)

Despite Thompson's call for urgency in the transfer market, Liverpool are continuing their lengthy pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola. Meanwhile, with owners Fenway Sports Group offloading a minority stake in the club for approximately £1.4billion last week, the former captain can envisage huge transfers materialising.

"The finance side of it, we could spend that money because we've done very, very well in sales," he added. "And when you look at it, just the investment in which we get into the football club, the likes of Liverpool and Manchester United, when you see them travelling the world, it shows that they are the two biggest football clubs.

‌



"People want to invest in them, so you have that, and I think it contributes towards a better buying power even with the restrictions that you have."

Regardless of who arrives at Anfield before the transfer window shuts, the team is entering a new era under the guidance of new manager Iraola. Seven-time league winner Thompson is optimistic that Iraola will win over Liverpool supporters, but has warned the ex-Bournemouth manager that he is facing a much different task.

‌



"Change can be good, change can be bad. You change because things have been going wrong - it's not like Jurgen Klopp leaving on a high," Thompson continued. "Things have gone wrong, so you need a new manager, new ideas, you need the players to tap into him as quickly as possible. Arne Slot came in and surprised us all by winning the league. The players invested in that from Jurgen Klopp.

"Hopefully this time there is a difference. We've got to get the intensity back; we've got to get the fans back on board, in which everything has been lost, and that's what he did at Bournemouth. [But] Bournemouth is not Liverpool. The big thing about it is that Bournemouth, a lot of the time, were almost the underdogs in games and played a lot of counter-attacking football.

"With Liverpool, one of the biggest problems is breaking down packed defences. This is where he's got to find that ingredient with someone like Florian Wirtz, where do you get the best out of him, and to have Alexander Isak firing, that can do them a lot of good."

Sports.title: Spurs agree £85m deal to sign Savinho from Man City
Sports.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have agreed an £85m deal with Manchester City to sign Savinho.

Spurs will pay an initial £75m for the Brazil international, with a further £10m available in add-ons.

It is understood £5m of the potential bonuses are effectively guaranteed, meaning City could receive at least £80m from the deal.

Savinho is set to undergo a medical ahead of completing his move to north London.

Spurs are also continuing talks with Manchester City over a separate deal for striker Omar Marmoush as they look to strengthen their attacking options further.

Brentford

Tottenham Hotspur Saturday 22nd August 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six first-team players this summer. They spent £185m on two midfielders, Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, from Newcastle and West Ham respectively.

Jan Paul van Hecke, meanwhile, joined from Brighton for £52m to replace Cristian Romero. Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka all arrived on free transfers.

Savinho, who has played a bit-part role since joining Manchester City in 2024, started only seven of his 24 Premier League appearances last season, in which he scored once and set up two goals.

How are Spurs spending so much money?

At the start of the transfer window, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge explained how Spurs are able to spend big this summer...

"We're told there are absolutely no concerns about falling foul of the Premier League's financial rules.

"The club is in great financial health after qualifying for Europe in 18 of the last 20 seasons. The revenue driven by the stadium is huge: boxing, concerts, NFL games - you name it.

"In fact, in the Deloitte Money League, the rankings show that Tottenham Hotspur have leapfrogged Chelsea to become the ninth richest club in the world with annual revenues of £549.2m.

"On top of that, Spurs are one of the clubs to benefit most from the Premier League's shift to squad cost ratio from PSR, which has just come into effect. But the reason we're seeing Spurs spend so much is a shift in strategy under new leadership.

"Daniel Levy left at the start of last season, and there's a real desire to spend the money to dine at the very top table.

"Now the new leadership and the owners promised fans, after avoiding relegation on the final day, that they would spend the club's revenue on the first team, and they are delivering on that."

'City will want to replace Savinho and Marmoush'

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom:

"Both players [Savinho and Marmoush] are essentially surplus to requirements at Manchester City. It's been pretty apparent through the summer. Enzo Maresca has said that in the case of both players, they are very much entitled to stay and fight for their first-team place.

Manchester City

Bournemouth Sunday 23rd August 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

"But equally he understands, a bit like James Trafford, when a player wants to play first-team football and they're not guaranteed the starting shirt, then the club, if they receive an offer that's acceptable, will not stand in their way. That applies to both players.

"City would need to replace these players. They would definitely, I'd say, have to replace one. They would like to and would aim to replace two.

"But the transfer window is closing in less than a fortnight. These are big positions to fill so late in the window."

Sports.title: Hadjar hopeful of Italian GP return after wrist injury
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar is hopeful he can return for the next Formula 1 race after a wrist injury forced him to miss this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix.

Hadjar suffered the injury while boxing in training during the summer break earlier this month and will be replaced by Liam Lawson, who becomes the first driver to race again for Red Bull having previously being dropped by the team.

Yuki Tsunoda will take over Lawson's seat at Racing Bulls alongside full-time driver Arvid Lindblad.

Sky Sports News understands Hadjar suffered a small crack in a bone in his wrist late last week in a routine workout before discussions with Red Bull medical staff led to the decision to miss the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort to allow more time for recovery before the next race at Monza.

Hadjar is at the track this weekend at Zandvoort to support Lawson and is hopeful of a return at the Italian Grand Prix, which takes place on September 4-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hadjar tells Karun Chandhok he's pleased with how he's performed alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull

Lawson: I'm much more comfortable compared to 18 months ago

Lawson was dropped from Red Bull after two disappointing races last year but did enough over the remainder of the 2025 season at Racing Bulls to retain his seat for this year.

The 24-year-old has been one of the stars in the midfield this season with eight points finishes and sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship - only behind the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers.

"I've had a lot more races since then [being dropped from Red Bull]. I feel much more comfortable racing in this sport, but it's going to be a very challenging weekend, for sure," said Lawson.

"It's a Sprint weekend, so it's going to be a quick learning process. But that's what we're focused on, that's what we tried to do in the simulator. If we can try and speed up that learning process as much as possible, then that would help our weekend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lawson sits down with Sky Sports F1's Crofty to reveal his the tracks he'd take with him to a desert island

Tsunoda has been watching from the sidelines this year and has an opportunity to impress to find a seat on the grid in 2027, albeit his options appear to be limited following the recent re-signings of Verstappen at Red Bull plus Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon at Williams.

The Japanese driver revealed he was on holiday in Greece before getting a call on Tuesday to get ready to drive for Racing Bulls.

"When I heard, I was like half excited, half still doubtful because anything can happen, but I was super excited too," he said.

Sports.title: Why a German football superstar is now playing in the third tier
Sports.content:
"Not normal." It is a phrase that Alexandra Popp turns to more than once when speaking after her debut for Borussia Dortmund. She has scored twice. The team has won 3-0. Nothing unusual there. But the crowd of 4,572 in Germany's third tier is new.

Popp is already a phenomenon here. The average attendance at Dortmund last season was below half the number at the atmospheric Stadion Rote Erde for this game against Arminia Bielefeld. Season ticket sales have almost tripled from 600 to 1700.

It is because Popp has come. This summer, the former captain of the Germany national team with 67 international goals to her name joined the club she supported as a girl. It is a homecoming that has captured the imagination among her fellow fans.

Image: Popp's Borussia Dortmund shirt is outselling many of the men

Her shirt is everywhere in Dortmund and not just among the growing fanbase for the women's team. Sales of the shirt that bears her name are currently outselling those of Serhou Guirassy, the top scorer for the men's team for each of the past two seasons.

Speaking to Popp after her match-winning display, she says: "It was a very nice atmosphere. We have more than 4,000 people here in the stadium and that is amazing. I played for so many years in the Bundesliga and some stadiums are not so full like that."

It is some transformation because Dortmund did not even have a women's team until 2020, by which point Popp was already a three-time champion of Europe and a six-time Bundesliga winner. Having started in the seventh tier, the club are now up to the third.

Image: Fans look on during the women's match between Borussia Dortmund and Arminia Bielefeld

In truth, the football is far beneath her level. When a cross was hung up into the penalty box late in the first half and Popp attacked the ball with her head, the outcome was as inevitable as watching Erling Haaland up against children. She was utterly unstoppable.

But this was an emotional move for a 35-year-old icon motivated by more than just the standard of football. "I had two choices," she explains. "To stay in Wolfsburg or switch to my favourite kid as a club, Borussia Dortmund. The decision did not take long."

Popp has a reputation for being a relatively stoical figure, a determined soul known for her drive and determination. But she admits the reaction to her arrival has been overwhelming. "It is wonderful. You see the heart of the club and the heart of the fans."

Image: Popp's move to Dortmund has captured the imagination

The chance to inspire is another reason for coming home. "I can develop something here." It was something of an embarrassment that the best supported team in European men's football did not have a women's team. They are trying to make up for lost time.

"It is a new challenge for me," she says. And for all her superiority, on this evidence, it might not be completely straightforward. "It was a tough game," she concedes. Arminia offered dogged resistance and Popp had to endure some particularly robust treatment.

"Some people told me before that it is possible I get some fouls. It is what it is." Two opposition players were booked for fouling Popp and it could and should have been many more. She tried to counter this by roaming all over the pitch in search of space.

Image: Popp speaking to reporters after scoring two goals on her Dortmund debut

"Everywhere," she replies, laughing, when asked by Sky Sports what position she was supposed to be playing in. "No, I have to play on the 10. But I am a player when I see there is some space or we need to defend or something, I take my legs and I run back."

Another consideration is how her mere presence at the club changes the dynamic for young team-mates who are unaccustomed to the world's media turning up at the old ground next to the cavernous Signal-Iduna Park that hosts the men's team.

Image: Popp is covering the ground for the team

"Some of them were a bit nervous," says Popp. There is Manuela Zinsberger, the former Bayern Munich and Arsenal goalkeeper, who on the evidence of this game is not likely to be too busy this season. But many others are living a new experience right now.

"We have a normal relationship," insists Popp. "The young girls speak with me all the time. They are not scared and that is very important. Sometimes even in the national team, the young girls are scared to tell me something. The girls here are very open."

Image: Popp during a public training session

Even without Popp, Dortmund had a goal difference of over 100 last season, somehow contriving not to win promotion as they missed out on top spot by two points - both of which were dropped in this corresponding fixture against Arminia last season in April.

This time around, it is unlikely to be an issue. Popp and Dortmund have big ambitions. "That is the first, the championship," she says. "I hope that we can make more steps. We have a dream to grow. We want to be in the first league as fast as we can."

And with that, Germany's three-time footballer of the year is off. There are autographs to sign, fans of all ages demanding selfies. Popp has signed a three-year contract. By then, the aim is to be back in the Bundesliga where she belongs. But Alex Popp is already home.
