Sports.title: Kevin Blake's 33/1 Nunthorpe pick: York day three tips
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake is back with two picks on day three of York's Ebor meeting, including a 33/1 Nunthorpe Stakes fancy.

The Ebor Festival at York will have reached the halfway stage by the time you read this. Hopefully the meeting has been good to you so far, but either way there is still plenty of excellent action to come.

The main event of the day is the Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (3:35). It hardly needs to be said at this stage, but the sprinting division is Europe has just been carnage for the last few years. Big-priced winners have consistently popped up and left punters scratching their heads and with the rain having arrived prior to this race, the scope for something unexpected happening seems all the greater.

So, considering that, I'm going to go right down the page in search of what I feel is the most captivating outsider and that is the Ralph Beckett-trained STARLUST. To say the five-year-old has a quirky profile would be underselling it, but bear with me.

Venture back two years in time and he was one of the better five-furlong performers on the scene, finishing a close third to Bradsell in this race, getting no luck when holding every chance in the Prix de l'Abbaye and gaining his biggest win in the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint at Del Mar.

Following his solid fourth in the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last year he was retired to stud in Australia where he got something like 70 mares in foal. However, his connections were not pleased with his fertility rate and made the unorthodox decision to return him to training with Ralph Beckett.

Image: Asfoora ridden by Oisin Murphy on their way to winning the Nunthorpe

Cases such as these don't always lead to racing careers being successfully revived, but it can happen, and there has been enough promise in the run-to-run progression of Starlust to suggest he is building to a big run.

He needed his return to action at Carlisle and the King Charles III Stakes didn't play out well for him at all, but he showed much more in a first-time visor when a never-nearer fourth in a Listed race over this course and distance last time.

It is worth noting that he has shown a particular liking for York in the past, including when there was plenty of ease in the ground, so if he is going to get competitive in Group 1 company again, this could be the day to chance him at a very big price.

The British Stallion Farms EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (4:45) is one of the most valuable maidens in the calendar and has duly attracted a very strong field. However, one of the newcomers or unexposed runners will need to be very good to get the better of the Aidan O'Brien-trained OKLAHOMA.

The son of Wootton Bassett is out of no less than Hydrangea and he made a really promising debut when second to the exciting Giant Sequoia with a bunch of subsequent winners in behind. He was sent off a very short price to make it second-time lucky in a maiden at Killarney, but he could only finish third in a race that has already worked out very well.

The addition of cheekpieces and this bigger track will both be a help to him and he can be expected to be tough to beat even in this strong company.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for as the new season kicks off
Sports.content:
1 Nwaneri out of Arsenal picture

While Myles Lewis-Skelly looks likely to remain at the Emirates, the same can’t be said for Ethan Nwaneri. The 19-year-old was outstanding in his breakthrough season for Arsenal in 2024-25 but barely featured last season and was sent on loan to Marseille. That didn’t really work out and Arsenal are now exploring another temporary move to ensure Nwaneri gets regular football this season. Milan, RB Leipzig, Dortmund and Fulham are all thought to be interested, with Nwaneri unlikely to feature on the bench for Friday’s opener against Coventry as a result. Whether Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are available remains to be seen as Arsenal attempt to find suitors for the Brazil duo. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 New United pair down for Tigers test

Manchester United’s summer transfer business has focused on recruiting in central midfield. It will be interesting to see who Michael Carrick selects in two key roles for the first game of the season. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been present for more of pre-season than Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute for England at the World Cup and was a late returner to Carrington after a holiday. Carlos Baleba surely will not have arrived in time to start at Hull. Mainoo is in the best position in the long term but if Carrick decides to ease him into the season, it would be intriguing to see how Santos and Tielemans team up, the stress test for a new partnership that could provide the perfect balance of defensive awareness and ability to move the team up the pitch. Will Unwin

Hull City v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Swapped pair face former clubs

Neither Everton nor Crystal Palace have enjoyed a particularly scintillating summer of transfer activity but combined to make headlines with a swap deal between Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson. The pair will face one another – and their former clubs - on the first weekend of the season, eager to prove what their worth to their new teams. McNeil was rarely a regular on Merseyside but had a positive second half to last season, ironically after a move to Crystal Palace fell through at the last minute. Johnson did not settle at Selhurst Park, unable to crack the code that would get him into the starting lineup on a weekly basis, after moving from Spurs. A fresh start should reinvigorate the duo and there is no better way to further boost the mood than beating a former employer. WU

Everton v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm

4 Can Ipswich copy Black Cats’ success?

Ipswich clearly learned a lot from what Sunderland did a year ago, as they went out and bought a lot of players. The Black Cats quickly moulded their 19 acquisitions into a successful unit but at least they had the positive of a head coach in Régis Le Bris who had his feet under the table. Gary O’Neil is the new man at Portman Road and he has 12 signings – at time of writing – to potentially use for the opener. The record arrival, Emersonn, who has moved to Portman Road from Toulouse, is the most eye-catching of those who have been acquired. The Brazilian has an underwhelming career goalscoring record and a few question marks hanging over his head. Even though it is their first game, Ipswich need to pick up points at home, and to do so require a striker who can cause problems for defenders. How quickly Emersonn adapts will be critical for the Tractor Boys’ success this year. WU

Ipswich Town v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Emersonn is one of a number of big-money signings made by promoted Ipswich this summer. Photograph: Keeran Marquis/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

5 Glasner’s tough Diomande ready for debut

August is the season for debuts and no one will be more satisfied than Oliver Glasner when Ousmane Diomande steps over the white line at the City Ground. Glasner wanted the Ivorian centre-back to replace Marc Guéhi at Crystal Palace, six months before the England defender departed for Manchester City. Diomande, a £34m buy from Sporting, is expected to line up in a back three for Nottingham Forest against Leeds, when the Austria midfielder Xaver Schlager, who played for Glasner at Wolfsburg, could also make his Forest bow. Diomande is a quick and physical defender but another aspect of his appeal is his aerial power at set pieces. “They’ve both played Champions League football and they are used to competing for titles,” said Glasner. “They can add this winning mentality.” Ben Fisher

Nottingham Forest v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

6 Serene Senesi can bring calm to Spurs

Cristian Romero has taken his maverick brand of defending to Atlético Madrid, upsetting neutral Premier League watchers. His compatriot Marcos Senesi has arrived to shore up things at the back as Roberto De Zerbi desperately tries to steer Spurs away from a third straight season of battling relegation. The all-action Romero had his qualities as a leader and defender but never felt dependable, which is what most want from a centre-back and captain. Senesi impressed during his time at Bournemouth, rarely making headlines but proving himself a calm presence at the back. The Argentinian is good on the ball and will be more adventurous in possession than his countryman. He is yet to be sent off in three seasons as a Premier League player – Romero was dismissed twice in 2025-26 alone, not to mention a one-match ban and a fine for his behaviour towards a referee. His calmness will improve Spurs. WU

Brentford v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Villa head south besieged by problems

It is surely not how Unai Emery envisaged the countdown to Aston Villa’s season-opener at Brighton on Sunday – and certainly not as he enjoyed the afterglow from the club’s Europa League triumph over Freiburg in May. The manager has an extraordinary number of problems. Take the midfield where the new signings João Gomes and Johan Manzambi are injury doubts. Note: Amadou Onana is a long-term casualty while Youri Tielemans has been sold. It goes on. Emery is about to lose Ezri Konsa to Arsenal – in a summer where Villa have also sold Morgan Rogers and Lucas Digne. They are trying to move on Emi Martínez, while the future of Ollie Watkins is uncertain, with Al-Hilal circling. For the cherry on top, the rampaging 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo is a fitness concern. Emery’s teamsheet will be very interesting. Will he pitch the new goalkeeper, Zion Suzuki, who only signed on Wednesday, straight in? David Hytner

Brighton v Aston Villa, Sunday 2pm

8 Maresca must win to silence City noise

Is Enzo Maresca already under pressure after Manchester City’s 3-0 schooling by Arsenal in the Community Shield? Maybe not, but if the Italian’s new team go down at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, you do not have to be a soothsayer to picture the scrutiny that will follow. Maresca and City are enduring a difficult transfer window, with Rodri’s departure to Barcelona the headline, a dizzying blow that has to be shaken off. The new Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, has faced City six times in the Champions League with Leipzig and Mönchengladbach, and is sure to order his visitors to go for the jugular at the Etihad. City are vulnerable but Maresca can remedy this with a win of any sort. This, after all, is the job many felt he was the obvious choice for. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Anything but a win for Manchester City at home to Bournemouth will increase scrutiny on Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Dimitris Legakis/EPA

9 King Kev remembered at Newcastle

Kevin Keegan was supposed to have been the guest of honour at St James’ Park on Sunday, but his death from cancer in July means this meeting of two of his old clubs will turn into a tribute to one of English football’s enduring heroes. Keegan’s family will be present to witness an outpouring of love for the former Liverpool and Newcastle forward and (twice) Magpies manager. Once the game kicks off, all eyes will be on Alexander Isak, a St James’ Park old boy whose decision to force a £125m move to Anfield last summer did not go down well on Tyneside. The Sweden striker, making his first return to Newcastle, has much to prove at Liverpool, and now has a new head coach to impress in Andoni Iraola. Newcastle too have a new face in the home dugout, where Matthias Jaissle will occupy the technical area for so long inhabited by Eddie Howe. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Liverpool, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Former Madrid managers meet in capital

Real Madrid’s two head coaches from last season meet at Craven Cottage, with the focus on Xabi Alonso, rather than Álvaro Arbeloa. The Fulham man, however, may have more to prove in the Premier League. His managerial career has been less prominent than that of his Basque rival – and he has clearly insisted on snapping up talent from the Bernabéu. Gonzalo García and César Palacios have made the trip over from the Spanish capital with Arbeloa. It shows great faith from the former Liverpool defender but it does put extra pressure on the trio, their fates now permanently intertwined. All three need a positive start to show they merit being in the Premier League. Otherwise, it would be very easily to criticise them individually and collectively. WU

Sports.title: Premier League returns and Arsenal sense opportunity with rivals in flux
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta wants to get his messaging absolutely right. According to him, Arsenal are not about to defend their Premier League title. They are set to attack another one.

Remember Win the dog, who the manager brought in to the club’s training ground a few years back? She must now be called “Won”. But it is when Arteta quibbles over another bout of semantics that he highlights why he is entering the new season with such energy and optimism.

Do not talk to him about Arsenal’s stability. He prefers the word “consistency” along with more thrusting ones like “ambition”. The overall theme is clear. When Arteta surveys the landscape at the top end of the English game, he sees a settled environment at his club and flux elsewhere.

In terms of the so-called Big Six – the richest clubs in the country, as ranked by Deloitte – there are new managers at Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea; a virtually new one at Tottenham and a relatively new one at Manchester United. It has been a summer of unprecedented change in the Premier League with nine clubs with a new man in charge. Of those who hold out hope of a title challenge, only Aston Villa have a fully bedded-in manager in Unai Emery.

Rather abruptly, Arteta finds himself as the longest-serving manager in the division; he took over from Emery at Arsenal in December 2019. Emery is second on the list, having been at Villa for three years and nine months, and only one other – Daniel Farke at Leeds – has been at his club for more than three years.

When Arteta was given the job at Arsenal, Pep Guardiola was two titles into his storied City tenure, Jürgen Klopp had won the Champions League at Liverpool and was on his way to winning the league that season and José Mourinho had just joined Spurs.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta and Arsenal held their nerve to hold off the challenge from Manchester City last season. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Arteta has seen them all off, with Guardiola’s departure from City at the end of last season being the most significant single shift in the dynamics for the forthcoming campaign.

Arteta is now the big beast, the only current manager to have won the Premier League, and as Arsenal prepare for the curtain-raiser at home to Coventry on Friday night, it is hard to ignore the confidence they are projecting. With virtually of all their rivals in transition, uncertainty undercutting the excitement, predictions difficult to make in the face of little actual evidence, Arsenal are reassured by their firm foundations. They sense opportunity, another title; the creation of a dynasty. That is the ultimate goal.

There is something more. Namely how everything changed for them in the closing weeks of last season. City had done the hard work, clawing back a nine-point deficit from the middle of March – a period when they had a game in hand. But in the five-match shootout that followed, City blinked first, drawing at Everton. Most know how nerve-racking it was for Arsenal. Not least Arteta. The Emirates Stadium was a sea of anxiety when Arsenal last played there – against Burnley in the penultimate game of the season. They got a 1-0 win over the line.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães is a high-quality arrival from Newcastle to boost Arsenal’s midfield ranks. Photograph: Mark Leech/Offside/Getty Images

Then City drew at Bournemouth and it was over; Arsenal’s 22-year wait, the oppressive weight. It is impossible to underestimate the feeling of liberation. Nobody can question the bottle of this team. Nobody will taunt them with the cry of “second again, olé, olé.” It is plain Arteta and his players will feed off it and perhaps it will lead to a more expansive style of football. The fear of falling short inhibited their game as the heat rose last time out.

Arsenal have made changes behind the scenes, looking for the marginal gains, most notably in the medical department where the head doctor, Zafar Iqbal, was mutually consented in early June. Arnaldo Abrantes has come in from Aston Villa to replace him. If the players can stay fitter for longer, Arsenal believe they can stay ahead. They have protected themselves with moves to deepen an already well-stocked squad. Bruno Guimarães is the most eye-catching addition, with Ezri Konsa about to follow.

Arsenal versus City still feels like the primary head-to-head. Guardiola had Arteta’s number last season, winning two and drawing one of the three meetings between the clubs. City were much the better team in the Carabao Cup final that they won 2-0. But that was under Guardiola and that was with Rodri and Bernardo Silva. If Guardiola’s exit has hit City the hardest, then those of the commanding midfielders to Barcelona and Real Madrid, respectively, is not far behind.

City’s faith in their new manager, Enzo Maresca, is rooted in what they saw of him when he worked on their coaching staff; he was an assistant to Guardiola in the treble-winning season of 2022-23. Previously, he coached the Under‑23s to the Premier League 2 title in 2020-21.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson has arrived at Manchester City for £116m, but, like his manager, he has big shoes to fill. Photograph: Alex Pantling/FA/Getty Images

It is a well-thought-through appointment; the kind a well-run club makes. Yet at the same time, it is not one to quicken the pulse. Maresca, quite simply, has enormous shoes to fill. Ditto Elliot Anderson, the impressive young midfielder upon whom City have bet the house. Can City be better given the personnel losses they have sustained? They must surely do so given the direction of travel at Arsenal. City do retain the cheat code that is Erling Haaland.

There are parallels between City and Liverpool, who want their new manager, Andoni Iraola, to have a similar impact in his first season that Arne Slot managed in 2024-25. Slot took Klopp’s team and glided to the title. Maybe consistency in the dugout is not everything?

On the other hand, Slot was given only one new player – Federico Chiesa – who barely played that season and he essentially stuck with what had made the Klopp collective so successful. It was evolution not revolution. When he tried the latter last season, Slot found that his tenure unravelled, although his rotten luck with injuries must be acknowledged. There was also the death of Diogo Jota.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool have moved on Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konaté and, most crucially, Mohamed Salah, even if he was a shadow of his former self last season. Salah has not yet been replaced; it would be impossible to replace the prime-years version of him and Iraola, who has a number of injury concerns, has it all to do.

Coaxing more from Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak is fundamental. Iraola’s style has the capacity to hold Anfield in thrall; the aggression, the front-foot slickness, the boldness to go one-versus-one all over the pitch. How quickly can he impose it?

Chelsea will be interesting under Xabi Alonso, who has been allowed to add players to fit into the 3-4-2-1 he used to such stunning effect at Bayer Leverkusen. Alonso has also been permitted to break from the club’s youth-first signing model and bring in much-needed experience.

View image in fullscreen Morgan Rogers celebrates scoring in pre-season, after his £117m move from Aston Villa. Photograph: Anthony Hanc/Wired Photos/Shutterstock

Morgan Rogers, alongside Cole Palmer and behind João Pedro, with Moisés Caicedo and maybe Reece James in the deep midfield roles, has a very nice feel to it. There is talent in central defence. The lack of European football will be a temporary blessing.

Ask any chief executive what supporters want at the start of a season and the answer is invariably the same: be better than last season. Which will not be a problem for Chelsea after the implosion to limp home in 10th. Or Spurs, who finished 17th for the second campaign in a row and narrowly avoided relegation. Roberto De Zerbi, who was appointed as the manager with seven games to go, kept them up and in the first summer since the end of Daniel Levy’s near 25-year as chair, the new hierarchy have been determined to act decisively. Their heavy spend on Premier League-proven players has allowed the fanbase to dream.

De Zerbi is a man to generate buy-in. In him they trust. Ditto a midfield that will feature Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. With Conor Gallagher or James Maddison expected to fill the No 10 role, Spurs look to have a proper unit to hold things together. They will also benefit from no European football.

What about United, for whom everything suddenly came together after the appointment of Michael Carrick in January, initially for an interim spell? His record meant the club had to give him the job on a permanent basis – he finished the season with 12 wins and three draws from 17 league matches. It was 2.3 points per game. Transpose that over a 38-match campaign and you get 87 points. Arsenal won the title with 85. Are United dark horses for glory?

Concerns remain. Carrick was largely untroubled by injuries and when United have their best XI on the field they are a match for anybody. When they miss a few, as they normally did under Ruben Amorim, they can flatline. United were always going to have to add a good number of signings this summer, particularly as they prepare to go from a Europe-free season to a return to the Champions League. They have not yet done enough; the final week-and-a-half of the transfer window could be crucial. As Mike Tyson almost said, everybody has a plan until they are punched in the face by the Champions League.

View image in fullscreen Marcus Rashford is back at Manchester United after falling out of favour during Ruben Amorim’s reign. Photograph: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA/Getty Images

Are Villa really about to take another step forward after the highs of last season when they finished fourth and won the Europa League? It feels unlikely given the departures, headlined by those of Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, with Konsa primed to go, too. Strangely, there is a whiff of transition about them. It is possible to find reasons to fret about every team. Apart from Arsenal.

Sports.title: Tottenham close on deals for Manchester City’s Savinho and Omar Marmoush
Sports.content:
Manchester City are close to agreeing the transfer of Savinho to Tottenham for £85m, with a separate deal of around £75m for the arrival of Omar Marmoush from the FA Cup-winners to the north London club also being worked on.

Savinho signed for the City Football Group in summer 2022 for 40m euros (£30.8m), first joining Troyes, so the prospective sale of the 22-year-old for £85m represents a near £55m profit for City’s owners. After loans at PSV and Girona, the Brazilian joined City two years ago but the winger failed to establish himself as a first-choice under Pep Guardiola, the former manager.

Marmoush was bought in January 2025 for around £59m but, as with Savinho, the Egyptian forward was not a regular starter under Guardiola, due to having to compete with Erling Haaland.

If Spurs do buy both Savinho and Marmoush, that would take the club’s investment in Roberto De Zerbi’s squad this summer to £387m, after the purchases of Sandro Tonali for £100m, Mateus Fernandes (£85m), and Jan Paul van Hencke (£52m).

Sports.title: PSG are the best team in Europe. The rest of Ligue 1 are just trying to survive
Sports.content:
On the eve of a new Ligue 1 season, many clubs seem a little distracted. Even those accustomed to competing at the top have concerns that transcend the pitch. In a league that contains the greatest team on the continent, the focus of the majority of clubs has shifted to surviving and providing, rather than competing.

Any fighting spirit has long since been kicked out of Paris Saint-Germain’s competitors; back-to-back Champions League titles will do that. It feels like a long time ago since Kylian Mbappé moved to Real Madrid on a free transfer, leaving behind a scent of opportunity that filled the nostrils of Marseille, Monaco and Lille. Roberto De Zerbi was bullish when he joined Marseille. “I’m not here to finish second,” said the manager, who has since moved to Tottenham. Finishing second has now become an aspiration, especially for a club such as Marseille, given their predicament.

Of all of the distracted teams, Marseille are the most preoccupied with off-field matters. While the club avoided a European ban, allowing them to compete in the Europa League this season, Uefa’s tone was one of a final warning: redress the financial imbalance or you’re out.

There has been a change in the dugout, with the (almost boringly) dependable Bruno Génésio coming in for Habib Beye, who replaced De Zerbi in February, but the demands made by Uefa – and the DNCG, French football’s financial watchdog – have prevented the club from making a single signing. There have been plenty of sales (Mason Greenwood, Facundo Medina, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Gérnoimo Rulli have all left on permanent deals), but not enough for Marseille to contemplate dipping into the market themselves.

Marseille’s “everything must go” sale suggested the club were in survival mode and their reaction to Pierre-Emile Højbjerg refusing a move to Newcastle confirmed it. He was stripped of the captaincy for the club’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Génésio said it was a decision made above his station and one he disagreed with. “I am an employee. I have to agree to certain obligations,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Pierre-Emile Højbjerg was stripped of the captaincy for Marseille’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Photograph: Icon Sport/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Génésio wants to keep Højbjerg, but the austerity cure ensures the club are hell-bent on doing the opposite. It is a situation that perfectly encapsulates the conflict between sporting ambition and financial necessity, familiar to many clubs in Ligue 1, and increasingly those competing towards the top of it – lest we forget Lyon’s recent brush with administration.

With the authorities “supervising their wage bill”, Monaco have made savings this summer. Maghnes Akliouche’s £43m move to PSG has been programmed for some time, and Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara may still bring in big fees before the end of the window. The unexpected sale of Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m has given the club more breathing room in their quest to cut costs and raise funds.

TV broadcasting rights are no longer the lifeblood of Ligue 1. Instead, French clubs rely on the reckless abandon of Premier League sides making multimillion-pound bets on unproven young players. Bamba had played 18 league games when Newcastle came with the big money. Ligue 1 has always been a ​stopover for its top talents, but the rate of churn has hit new levels. Liverpool did not wait around before signing Jérémy Jacquet and Mamadou Sangaré only needed one campaign at Lens to convince Brentford he was worth an expensive bet.

Even those in stronger financial health cannot resist advances. The prospect of coaching Lens in the Champions League could not prevent Pierre Sage from crossing the Channel to join Crystal Palace. Sangaré made a similar journey, while Adrien Thomasson, Malang Sarr, Allan Saint-Maximin and Wesley Saïd – all instrumental in Lens’ second-place finish and maiden Coupe de France triumph last season – have been lured away. Success can be a poisoned chalice. At least their rebuild, under Dino Toppmöller, looks intelligent. You’d expect nothing less from Lens, but their pillaging once again exposes the limits to success in Ligue 1 for clubs that do not go by the name PSG.

View image in fullscreen Allan Saint-Maximin celebrates after scoring for Lens in the Coupe de France semi-final against Toulouse. He has now moved to MLS. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

The reigning champions, who are in search of a sixth consecutive league title, have often been accused of being distracted by the Champions League. When you win it two years in a row, you can justify it, but after their close race with Lens last season it isn’t an accusation that can be levelled at them this summer. Their starting XI is already the best in the league and beyond, so PSG’s transfer guru, Luís Campos, has focused on improving the second string that more often than not will be trotted out in Ligue 1.

Ferran Torres, Akliouche and Mika Godts are upgrades on the departing trio of Gonçalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in and Randal Kolo Muani, even if they will struggle to dislodge the current starters in the PSG attack. Lucas Digne is a shrewd pick as back-up to Nuno Mendes, too.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

PSG will probably have an easier ride in the league this season as the teams chasing them have either regressed or stagnated. Rennes, who must this season contend with European football for the first time in three seasons, are the only side that finished in the top seven last season that – on paper – look stronger than they were at the start of the summer.

Wealth immunises Rennes, to a degree, but Strasbourg are weaker after losing important players to Chelsea. Emanuel Emegha, the club captain, has been followed out the door by Valentín Barco, with the goalkeeper Mike Penders returning to his parent club after a loan spell at the Meinau. The latter has been replaced by Filip Jörgensen, who will have to play a “crucial role”, in the words of their new manager, Hugo Oliveira, formerly assistant to Marco Silva at Fulham. Time will tell if Jörgensen is up to the task; he was surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge so it may be a move born out of convenience. In any case, he will be busy if pre-season is anything to go by; Strasbourg have conceded 21 goals in their seven friendlies.

The managerial upheaval, from Liam Rosenior to Gary O’Neil, and now to Oliveira, also contributes to a feeling of instability at Strasbourg, one of 10 clubs part of a multi-club model in Ligue 1 this season. That, in itself, adds a feeling of “Who is this even for?” to the upcoming season. Not all clubs in these models are subservient, but nor do their own interests always guide decisions.

Rosenior knows all about that. The new Paris FC manager is one of two coaches returning to France in search of redemption following failed stints in England, with the former Southampton head coach Will Still joining Auxerre. There are also some more adventurous appointments, in the form of Davide Ancelotti at Lille and Filipe Luís at Monaco. There have been an incredible 12 managerial changes in France’s top flight for this season: plenty of change, even if some things will almost certainly stay the same.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick to Liverpool? Arsenal to swap Martinelli for Yildiz?
Sports.content:
After Vinícius Júnior signed a shiny new deal at Real Madrid, Arsenal are having to look elsewhere for a new winger. Turkey’s Kenan Yildizm who plies his trade with Juventus, is of interest to Mikel Arteta and the Gunners hierarchy. One potential way of getting the deal done is to send Gabriel Martinelli in the opposite direction.

It is all fun and games at Manchester City where they are trying to rebuild a midfield inside a week. Adam Wharton is supposedly on their wishlist but with a £100m price tag, the expense could be a little too much. City have reportedly put in a call to Selhurst Park but received a swift rebuffing in response. Considering the proximity of that Sainsbury’s to the Palace ground, any potential purchase of a midfielder would come with a lot of Nectar points. With Savinho on his way to Tottenham, City could replace him with Allan Elias, a left-footed right winger at Palmeiras – a team not keen on selling. Ruben Amorim is eager on a return to Manchester but only to take Rúben Dias to Milan.

Over at Anfield there are plans afoot for Liverpool to bid £55m for Endrick to test Real Madrid’s mettle on the matter. The Brazilian spent time on loan at Lyon last season and was recently linked with Aston Villa, who could re-enter the race should Ollie Watkins head to Al-Hilal.

There is still a good chance of a Chelsea clearout, with Nicolas Jackson chatting with Napoli over a move to Italy, while Atlético Madrid are also keen. Palace are in the market for a centre-back and are keen on signing up Blues bomb squad member Axel Disasi. The Frenchman is unwanted at Stamford Bridge, so would be a relatively straightforward signing after previous loan spells with Aston Villa and West Ham. Auxerre’s Kevin Danois is another player Pierre Sage likes the look of, with the 22-year-old midfielder marketed at £25m.

On thing that could sour the mood at Selhurst Park is the departure of frontman Jean-Philippe Mateta who is getting admiring glances from Tottenham. The Frenchman has been tipped to move on for a while and is into the final year of his contract, which could force Palace to cash in.

The latest news from Hull’s transfer tombola has linked them to Oussama Targhalline of Feyenoord. A bid has already been faxed to the Netherlands but Porto, Atalanta and Bologna are also in in pursuit of the midfielder.

Leeds, Liverpool and Everton are in the hat for Midtjylland winger Darío Osorio. The Chilean shown great promise in Denmark and the Europa League, and could become one of the finds of the window if someone stumps the cash. If you like a bit of niche on your bingo card, then Polish side Radomiak Radom having a loan offer for Leeds youngster Alfie Cresswell rejected is right up there.

Sports.title: New rules, managers and pundits: what’s different this Premier League season?
Sports.content:
The 2026-27 Premier League season kicks off on Friday and while the familiar rivalries return, the English top flight has some alterations this campaign. From evolved rules to new faces and broadcast changes, there is plenty to catch up on before a ball is kicked.

Law changes

The Premier League has some law and rule changes this season and the first will lead to a crackdown on time wasting.

Referees will be able to start a countdown of five seconds if they believe players are ticking down the clock during throw-ins and goal-kicks. If players take more than five seconds once the countdown has been enforced, the goal-kick becomes a corner and the throw-in is reversed.

That is not all that is being done to cut time-wasting. Last season, if a player was injured and play stopped as a result, they had to leave the pitch for 30 seconds. In this campaign, it will be increased to a minute and the only exceptions will be if a foul that received a card led to the injury, or other unusual circumstances.

There will also be a change to limit tactical timeouts by goalkeepers going down injured. If they do, a manager must choose another player to leave the pitch for one minute. Substitutions will also need to take just 10 seconds; if a player takes longer than that to leave the pitch, his replacement will not be able to come on for a further minute.

There will also be changes to video assistant referee interventions. VARs will now be able to intervene on second yellow cards if they have been shown in error. They cannot, however, tell a referee to issue a second yellow if one is not shown.

VARs will also be able to get involved where an attacking foul happens before a set piece is taken which leads to a penalty, a goal or a disciplinary sanction. They will be able to intervene to have the set piece retaken.

Despite players being given red cards for speaking to opposition players with their mouths covered at the World Cup this past summer, this is not a rule that will be adopted by the Premier League.

Managerial appointments

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso at Chelsea is one of nine new managers at the start of the Premier League campaign. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Crystal Pix/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

This season the defending champions, Arsenal, will have the longest-serving manager in the Premier League. Mikel Arteta has been in charge since 2019 and delivered his first title last season; Aston Villa’s Unai Emery is second on the list, with Leeds’ Daniel Farke third.

The upcoming campaign will set a record for the most new managers at the start of a Premier League season. The nine new names in the dugout are:

Marco Rose – Bournemouth

Xabi Alonso – Chelsea

Pierre Sage – Crystal Palace

Álvaro Arbeloa – Fulham

Gary O’Neil - Ipswich Town

Andoni Iraola – Liverpool

Enzo Maresca- Manchester City

Matthias Jaissle – Newcastle

Oliver Glasner – Nottingham Forest

View image in fullscreen Álvaro Arbeloa will take charge of Fulham after Marco Silva left to join Benfica. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

Biggest signings

There have been hundreds of signings in this summer’s transfer window and many have caught fans’ attention. Here are five to keep an eye on for this upcoming season:

Elliot Anderson: Nottingham Forest to Manchester City For a short time this summer, Anderson’s £116m move to Manchester City was a record transfer for a British player. The signing comes as part of City’s renovated midfield, with Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders leaving the club.

Morgan Rogers: Aston Villa to Chelsea The versatile forward was the player to eclipse Anderson’s record. Chelsea paid £117m for the Aston Villa star, who alongside Anderson helped England finish third at the World Cup. The 24-year-old is a huge loss for Villa; Rogers scored 10 goals and made seven assists in the Premier League last season.

Bruno Guimarães: Newcastle to Arsenal This move was an astute one for the Premier League holders. Guimarães is an experienced and reliable midfielder who will add depth to Arsenal’s engine room. Arsenal’s sporting director, Andrea Berta, said: “With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães will add experience and adaptability to Arsenal’s midfield. Photograph: Adrian Dennis/AFP/Getty Images

Gonzalo García: Real Madrid to Fulham García became a regular first-team presence for Real Madrid last season, and he has followed his manager for the second half of that campaign, Álvaro Arbeloa, to Fulham. Leaving Madrid for the first time, the highly rated striker needs to adapt quickly to the Premier League.

Thomas Meunier: Lille to Sunderland Sunderland have signed an experienced international in Meunier. The former PSG and Dortmund defender has amassed 83 caps for Belgium and won 14 trophies across his club career.

New kids on the block (or are they?)

The three promoted clubs all have plenty of Premier League history: Hull City, Coventry City and Ipswich Town.

The Tractor Boys won promotion in 2024 but were relegated the following season. Kieran McKenna managed to regain the club’s Premier League status after finishing second in the Championship. He will not be joining them in the top flight, though, as he stepped down to take a break from management. That means Gary O’Neil is back in the Premier League after last taking charge of Wolves.

View image in fullscreen Gary O’Neil is back in the Premier League in charge of newly promoted Ipswich. Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Hull were last in the top flight in 2016-17 and their first season there in a decade will be overseen by Sergej Jakirovic, who steered them to an unexpected promotion.

Coventry have spent 25 years out of the top flight and even dropped down to League Two. They have fought their way back up the pyramid with Frank Lampard engineering their Championship-winning campaign. The former Chelsea player and manager will lead the team this season, his first managerial position in the Premier League since his caretaking stint at the Blues in 2023.

Television and radio

Sky Sports and TNT Sports will remain the live TV broadcasters for the Premier League in the UK, with the BBC showing highlights on Match of the Day, but there are some slight changes this season.

The Premier League will allow on-field discussions between players and referees to be aired during live broadcasts. This will be trialled first and will not be present during the opening weekend.

Match of the Day will feature new pundits in the former Brentford and Spurs manager Thomas Frank, plus former players Toby Alderweireld, Robbie Keane and Ashley Young.

The BBC will no longer be airing its fantasy Premier League podcast Fantasy 606. The broadcaster Alistair Bruce-Ball confirmed the news in July, saying: “It’s our amazing listeners’ contributions who really made it. Thank you for listening, for sending your emails, your poems, your songs and for managing the listeners’ teams – we are really going to miss it!”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino eyes junior tournament in Dominican Republic as potential route out of crisis
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino wants to split the European and North American coalition that is seeking to oust him by attending a junior tournament in the Dominican Republic this weekend in another gamble to cling on to power from the Fifa president.

The Guardian has learned that Infantino has made plans to attend the U14 Boys Challenge competition organised by the Caribbean Football Union (CFU), 21 of whose associations are voting members of Fifa, despite being urged to stay away from the event by senior figures within Concacaf – the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football – which is working with Uefa to remove him.

Infantino will come face-to-face with the man widely viewed as his most credible challenger, the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, if he follows through with his intention to travel to the Dominican Republic, whose FA invited him to attend before the World Cup sell-off plan emerged last month.

The Dominican Republic has since backed the joint Uefa, Concacaf and Asian Football Confederation statement calling for Infantino to hold an independent review of the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, as well as an emergency meeting of the Fifa council.

Infantino has largely fallen back on the support of his most steadfast allies by spending time in Morocco and Qatar as the storm has raged over the last month, but is understood to view the CFU meetings as a good opportunity split the Concacaf block and lobby for votes from the region’s smaller nations before next March’s presidential election.

Concacaf’s most successful nation, Mexico, is defying the confederation by backing Infantino, who has also received support from two CFU members, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis.

View image in fullscreen Victor Montagliani, the Concacaf president, will be at the tournament in the Dominican Republic. Photograph: Omar Vega/Getty Images

The Boys Challenge and CFU meetings are not Fifa events, so Infantino’s plan to attend has raised eyebrows. Fifa declined to comment when asked about the president’s movements.

Uefa, Concacaf and the AFC are continuing to explore calling for a vote of no confidence in Infantino, which would bring the matter to a head before next year’s election.

Under Fifa’s statutes, its council can convene an extraordinary congress at any time if 43 of Fifa’s 211 member associations submit a written request specifying the items they want on the agenda, which can include no-confidence votes.

An extraordinary congress must then be convened within three months, although the governing body’s statutes contain no specific provision regarding a vote of no confidence in its president.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Infantino came under renewed pressure on Thursday with worldwide fans’ groups launching a petition calling for his resignation.

Fans are being encouraged to sign the petition, which already has support from all six Fifa confederations spanning continental and national fan groups.

“The shameful attempt by one individual – the Fifa president himself – to sell off the World Cup to private investors exposed a betrayal football will never forget,” a statement on behalf of the fan organisations said. “Infantino’s plan was stitched together in secret. Negotiated behind closed doors. Hidden from Fifa’s own members and from the millions of people whose passion makes football what it is.

“A president who repeatedly betrays football and makes a mockery of our game has lost the right to lead it,” the statement continued. “For the credibility of Fifa – and for the future of the game – he must resign.”

Sports.title: Adrian Durham: Tottenham will regret sale because Arsenal will sign next Harry Kane by 2027
Sports.content:
Adrian Durham: Tottenham will regret sale because Arsenal will sign next Harry Kane by 2027

Tottenham have been warned they have 'sold Harry Kane' all over again by offloading Will Lankshear.

That is according to talkSPORT host Adrian Durham, who has tipped the 21-year-old striker for an England call-up and then the unthinkable by joining Mikel Arteta's Arsenal.

5 Spurs have been warned they have made the 'biggest transfer mistake ever' by selling Lankshear Credit: Getty

Lankshear was sold by Spurs to Championship promotion favourites Middlesbrough last month.

The England Under-21 international joined Boro on a five-year deal for an initial £10million plus a potential £10m in add-ons this summer.

He has since scored three goals in two competitive outings, with Lankshear the only player to score for the club so far this term.

His strikes have secured wins over Wrexham and Lincoln City in the Carabao Cup and Championship, respectively.

Spurs' biggest transfer mistake

Having previously scored 11 league goals for Oxford United on loan despite their relegation last term, Durham is expecting big things for the young centre forward.

He has even predicted an historic Three Lions selection within the next 12 months.

Speaking on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Fiery Fridays podcast, Durham warned Spurs they could regret selling him.

Beginning his argument, he explained: "Spurs selling Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough, I think will go down as the worst mistake any Premier League club has ever made.

"I think even by the end of this season, Spurs will be regretting what I think is a crazy decision.

"Lankshear will play for England before the season is out. He’ll be an Arsenal player this time next year. For the second time in their recent history, Spurs have just sold Harry Kane."

5 Kane was sold by Tottenham to Bayern for £86m in 2023 and has thrived in Germany Credit: AFP

5 Although Kane wanted to leave in order to win trophies, Spurs' decision to sell Lankshear to Boro has been compared to letting Kane leave the club Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Spurs sold all-time leading scorer Harry Kane to Bayern Munich in a deal worth more than £100million in 2023.

Kane briefly played in an Arsenal youth team before joining boyhood club Spurs, with Lankshear having a similar trajectory. Born in 2005, he was initially in Arsenal's academy but joined Sheffield United in 2021.

Spurs then moved and snapped up Lankshear for £1m in 2022.

He went on to make just six first-team appearances, though, scoring once, alongside loan spells at West Brom and Oxford.

Harry Kane comparison

Durham is convinced Lankshear's goals are exactly what Spurs could be missing this term.

He continued: "Unless Spurs add goals before the end of the transfer window [on 1 September], they will be watching Will Lankshear, their product, smash in 20 plus [goals] for Boro, wishing he could be doing the same for them because Tottenham will need ways to find the back of the net.

5 Lankshear has scored three goals in two appearances since joining Boro Credit: Getty

"Last season, Lankshear scored double figures for a poor side in the Championship. His numbers at Oxford United were better than anything Harry Kane achieved in his loan spells as a young Spurs player.

"What I like about his play is, if you’ve not seen him play, he’s not just goals. He’s got many qualities. I’ve seen him described as a penalty box striker and he converts chances, he is a finisher for sure.

"Like any striker, most of his goals are scored in the box. I’ve seen him score from distance. He’s capable of the spectacular. He’s calm, movement is a bit special, strong, good in the air. He makes terrific runs. He can assist as well."

Spurs scored just 48 goals in 38 Premier League matches last term as they finished 17th, avoiding relegation by two points.

Although they are in talks to sign both Savinho and Omar Marmoush, Roberto De Zerbi has yet to make an attacking signing this summer.

Lankshear tipped for England and Arsenal

As for Lankshear, Durham believes the England youth international will earn a senior call-up, becoming the first outfield Championship player to do so since Wilfried Zaha in 2012.

5 Durham has tipped the former Spurs forward for an England call-up and Arsenal transfer in the next 12 months Credit: Getty

Lankshear could also succeed Viktor Gyokeres as Arsenal's No.9 ahead of next term, Durham admits.

Concluding his vision for the Boro frontman, he added: "Arsenal won’t put up with Gyokeres much longer and they’ll be in the market for a goalscorer and Lankshear will become a Arteta project like [Christos] Tzolis, the signing of the summer on the wing.

"I think that he will become the next Mikel Arteta vanity project and he’ll make it work as Lankshear is that good.

"Biggest transfer mistake ever. The kid from Spurs’ academy is going to become a legendary Arsenal and England striker.

"Just watch him go this season and watch Spurs tears as he fires in the goals for Boro."

Sports.title: ‘Luckiest manager in football’ will be the first one sacked in the Premier League this season
Sports.content:
‘Luckiest manager in football’ will be the first one sacked in the Premier League this season

Enzo Maresca will be the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, he's lucky to succeed Pep Guardiola.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook with Maresca making an underwhelming start to his tenure at the club.

5 Maresca's debut on the City touchline ended in resounding defeat Credit: Getty

City were beaten 3-0 in a resounding defeat by Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield last weekend.

Crook described them as 'all over the place defensively' and hinted that selling James Trafford to Leeds United may have been a mistake as Gianluigi Donnarumma had a performance to forget in goal.

With the Premier League returning on Friday night when Arsenal host Coventry City, live on talkSPORT, we have brought back Fiery Fridays to help preview the 2026/27 season.

Maresca tipped for the axe at City

And for his hot take, Crook declared that Maresca faces the very real possibility of being the first dismissal in the English top flight.

He believes the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss is fortunate to have been named as City's replacement for the legendary Guardiola and, given how they played against Arsenal, are not title contenders.

"I don't want to be over-reactionary to what we saw in Cardiff on Sunday but, if I was a Manchester City fan... I would be deeply concerned about Enzo Maresca," he said.

"I think there's a strong argument to say Maresca will be the first managerial departure of the season. He's got some competition because Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham looks an appointment, to me, that is fraught with danger.

"Regis Le Bris was under pressure at Sunderland towards the end of last season before qualifying for Europe, and I fear they might have a really difficult second season in the Premier League.

"But, this is the argument for Maresca. First and foremost, he might be the luckiest manager in football to land the job as successor to the great Pep Guardiola.

"You look at his track record - Leicester City walked the Championship under his tutelage, as they should when you look at the players at his disposal. But the fans weren't happy with the style of play, they didn't enjoy watching that Leicester City team.

5 Crook has predicted Maresca to be the first managerial dismissal Credit: Getty

5 He believes Maresca is lucky to have replaced Guardiola, who won six league title at City Credit: Getty

"Then he up sticks for Chelsea, wins the Club World Cup - which was a glorified pre-season friendly, let's be honest - wins the Conference League, which Chelsea should never have been playing in in the first place.

"Limps into the Champions League at the end of his first full season in charge. There was a danger, going into that final day, they wouldn't qualify for that competition. Falls out with the hierarchy.

"Again, the fans are not particularly enamoured with his style of football, and now he finds himself at Manchester City, inheriting this supposedly great team that Pep Guardiola left behind.

"But I'm not sure it is that great a team when you look at the departures - John Stones. Alright, he didn't play a lot of football last season but has been a massive part of their success.

"Bernardo Silva. Stuart Pearce said he is his favourite player in the Premier League. Again, so essential to what they achieved.

"Rodri. The driving force, the heartbeat in that team. No coincidence that when he's been injured for the last couple of seasons, they didn't manage to win the Premier League title.

5 Rodri's move to Barcelona could have a big impact on City's chances of success Credit: Getty

"Now they're going to cash in on Omar Marmoush (to Tottenham) as well. I know Adrian (Durham) said (Will) Lankshear (who joined Middlesbrough from Spurs) is a better player than Omar Marmoush, but who's going to fill in for Erling Haaland if Marmoush is sold?

"They don't have another striker on their books and, as far as I'm told going into the last two weeks of the window, that isn't a priority position.

"They're looking to bring in midfielders, we think (Ayyoub) Bouaddi is going to sign from Lille but he's a very young player.

"Enzo Fernandez, one of the most hated men in the Premier League, I still think that deal could happen but maybe that brings more baggage than Maresca realises at this moment in time.

"He wants Pedro Neto, is he a massive upgrade on Savinho? I'm not sure on what we saw in the second half of last season. So, this looks a really bang average Manchester City team to me.

"I got fooled, I think. When I did my predictions a couple of weeks ago, I had them as second, I must be mad! Because based on what we saw at the weekend, they're not going to finish anywhere near second.

5 Crook even went as far as to call Maresca a 'Temu Pep' Credit: Getty

"Then you speak to Maresca after the game, and he's almost too laid-back, he just doesn't seem to have that intensity and that fire that Guardiola had.

"I think maybe he realises he's a 'Temu Pep' and he's lucky to be in this position so, if they start the season poorly, and Bournemouth at home (on Sunday) is not an easy game by the way.

"I was down there this week and they feel pretty confident. Marco Rose, the new manager, carries himself with an air of authority that maybe Maresca doesn't have at this moment in time.

"Marco Rose, arguably, has got more experience at the top level than the man he's going to come up against at the weekend.

"I think if they start the season poorly, he's going to find himself bang under pressure, particularly if the football's not great. He shackled Nico O'Reilly at the weekend, that was noticeable.

"Under Pep, O'Reilly, despite the fact he was playing at left-back, his job was to push up and make the extra man in midfield. He sat so deep in that Community Shield, so I think there's a subtle difference in the style of play as well.

"And, these owners are ruthless. They didn't have to be under Guardiola because he was winning trophies season after season. But if you go back to his predecessors, (Roberto) Mancini was sacked (after) they lost the (2013) FA Cup final to Wigan.

"Manuel Pellegrini also won the Premier League title, he was sacked, they didn't mind turfing him out on his ears.

"So, they're not going to stand for average results this season, these Manchester City owners. That's my case for Enzo Maresca being the first head on the chopping board."

Sports.title: Frank Lampard bust-up against Arsenal sparked career-long feud as Jose Mourinho played peacemaker
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard has a heated history with Arsenal ahead of his latest trip to north London.

The former Chelsea midfielder takes his newly-promoted Coventry City side to the Emirates Stadium this weekend.



5 Lampard returns to Arsenal on Friday almost two decades on from the start of a career-long feud Credit: Getty

Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence at home to the Sky Blues on Friday at 8pm, live on talkSPORT.

Lampard has won just one of his six previous matches against the Gunners as a manager, a 2-1 win with Chelsea in December 2019.

However, it was a meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal during his playing career which sparked an 11-year feud which extended beyond his retirement.



Arsenal clash sparks Lampard feud

It stemmed from the 2007 League Cup final between the two sides in at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

The Blues ran out 2-1 winners thanks to a brace from Didier Drogba in the Welsh capital.



Their victory threatened to be marred by a stoppage time brawl involving players from both sides, including Lampard.

His involvement in the melee saw him clash with Arsenal's Cesc Fabregas, leading to a long-running feud between the pair.



The scuffle had broken out after Kolo Toure reacted furiously to a challenge from Chelsea substitute John Obi Mikel.

Lampard and Fabregas were the first to join the scene, with the latter dragging his rival away by his neck.

This prompted a fresh bust-up before coaching staff rushed onto the field from both benches in a bid to restore order.

5 Lampard and Fabregas were involved in a scuffle during the 2007 League Cup final Credit: Getty



Managers Jose Mourinho, who ran onto the pitch, and Arsene Wenger were amongst those to attempt to calm their players.

Words were exchanged between Lampard and Fabregas on the pitch before referee Howard Webb regained control of proceedings.

Both players were booked, whilst red cards were shown to Mikel, Toure and Emmanuel Adebayor, for allegedly striking Wayne Bridge.

However, the repercussions would continue beyond the final whistle as Lampard's feud with Fabregas lasted beyond the end of his playing days in 2017.



Lampard's rivalry with Fabregas

He even revealed it played a part in his Chelsea exit in 2014, with the club's all-time leading scorer released a month before Fabregas was signed.

The Spaniard was ultimately signed as Lampard's replacement, with the pair meeting once more in a 1-1 draw between Manchester City and Chelsea in September 2014, with the ex-Blues hero scoring.

5 Then Chelsea boss Mourinho even came onto the pitch to calm the tensions between players Credit: Getty

Lampard reflected on their rivalry in 2017, telling BT Sport, now TNT Sports: "We never played together. They let me go to get Cesc in.



"Me and Cesc never really got on well on the pitch so they didn't think we could share a dressing room."

In total, they played against each other a total of 21 times during their careers, with Lampard winning 11 matches compared to Fabregas' four.

The former Arsenal midfielder also confirmed their feud stemmed from the League Cup final.

Speaking to The Telegraph in 2020, he explained: "It’s completely true [that we fell out], we don’t have to hide anything, I think he will tell you the same thing.



"We have had many, many battles during the years and we kind of disliked each other on the football pitch because he wanted to play and win for Chelsea and I wanted to win for Arsenal.

5 Lampard revealed the bust-up prompted an 11-year feud with Fabregas which lasted beyond his retirement Credit: Getty

"The League Cup final was kind of crazy. We were losing 2-1 and it was basically the last moment of the game and you feel a little frustrated.

"[John Obi] Mikel and Kolo Toure went into a tackle and both got sent off. Me and Frank had a moment there.



"I think maybe I was very young and very enthusiastic. I wanted to beat the world basically and sometimes I was overwhelmed by the situation and went over the top."

Lampard and Fabregas end feud

It would not be until the 2018 World Cup that Lampard and Fabregas would finally bury the hatchet.

With the duo both working as pundits for the BBC during the tournament in Russia, they crossed paths at a gym.

Fabregas recalled: "We met each other at the World Cup in Russia working for the BBC and we went to the gym together.



5 The pair clashed again despite moving clubs before settling their rivalry in a Russian gym in 2018 Credit: Getty

"We were having lunch together and that was when he had just signed for Derby [as manager], and I was asking him questions about how he saw the situation and he was explaining his plans a little bit."

They could one day renew their rivalry in the dugout, with Fabregas now in charge of Serie A side Como following his appointment in 2024.

For now, though, Lampard will be looking to spoil the opening night for reigning champions Arsenal.
